2125: Title: How AI is reshaping the path from junior to senior developer
2126: URL: https://www.weforum.org/stories/artificial-intelligence/as-ai-reshapes-entry-level-software-jobs-where-will-senior-developers-come-from/
2127: Published: 2026-08-17T00:00:00.000Z
2128: Author: N/A
2129: Highlights:
2130: - Artificial intelligence (AI) may improve short-term productivity but it is cutting off the pipeline that creates future senior talent.
2131: - As AI absorbs routine tasks, companies must cultivate technical craft, domain knowledge, architecture, judgment and the ability to orchestrate AI systems.
2132: - Training needs to evolve as quickly as the work itself with employers and educators redesigning early-career development around production experience, domain expertise, judgment and AI-enabled ways of working.
2133: ...
2134: That pattern is worth paying attention to before it becomes a shortage. In the Dev Barometer Q2 2026, a survey of over 1,500 developers across 77 countries, 54% of senior developers agreed that AI is making the junior role less relevant.
2135: 
2136: The institutional knowledge that senior developers carry has traditionally depended on a pipeline of juniors moving through the same experiences beneath them. That pipeline is thinning. The industry is beginning to map what replaces it and the emerging answer has three layers, each tied to a different view of where value will concentrate next.
2137: ...
2138: ## CTOs: 3 bets on what replaces the traditional junior-senior developer pipeline
2139: 
2140: The roundtable participants’ responses clustered around three views on what comes after the traditional junior-senior developer pipeline, each one redefining the notion of seniority.
2141: 
2142: The first camp thinks of it as a development problem. They see senior developers shaped through apprenticeship, code review, production incidents and years of learning how a business actually works. They think cutting the junior funnel defers the cost and guarantees a premium later.
2143: 
2144: The second sees the challenge as a design problem. Junior roles are not disappearing; what they’re asked to do is changing. AI absorbs the routine tasks that used to fill a developer's first years of experience.
2145: 
2146: What they should be trained on instead is the domain itself, whether that’s the customer, the business model or the regulatory environment. As one CTO framed it, “technology stacks turn over but domain knowledge compounds.”
2147: 
2148: The third calls it a structural shift. As AI takes on a greater share of the build-and-ship layer, value shifts to decision-making, architecture and domain knowledge. Tomorrow's senior software developer is an orchestrator who directs AI agents and encodes institutional knowledge into documented processes. Seniority becomes the ability to govern a digital workforce.
2149: 
2150: I don’t see these as competing bets. They are three layers of the same investment in craft, domain understanding and judgment. All three warn that AI productivity metrics can hide a thinning pipeline.
2151: ...
2152: ## Senior developers: Technical competencies are still key
2153: 
2154: The same survey reveals something that cuts across all three perspectives. When we asked senior developers which skill matters most for a junior developer in the AI era, critical thinking was the top response at 25%, ahead of AI literacy at 18%.
2155: 
2156: Fundamental knowledge and problem decomposition also ranked prominently, suggesting that senior developers greatly value reasoning skills that support effective AI use.
2157: 
2158: Junior developers showed a similar instinct.
2159: 
2160: Forty-eight percent chose analytical thinking and problem-solving as the most valued skill on the job market today, nearly three times the 18% who chose proficiency in AI tools.

REVIEW-001 Slick-greeter written for a wallpaper deleted from the repo — broken login screen, reported as OK
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/xfce/setup.sh:175-194
- Severity: CRITICAL
- Category: Correctness
- Finding: Guard at 175 detects missing wallpaper, but the config write at 181 runs **unconditionally**, and line 194 prints `OK` unconditionally — even if `sudo tee` itself failed.
  ```
  175: if [ -f "$REPO/background.jpg" ]; then
  179:     WARN "$REPO/background.jpg missing — wallpaper skipped (see setup.md Section 7)"
  181: sudo tee /etc/lightdm/slick-greeter.conf >/dev/null <<'EOF'
  183: background=/usr/share/backgrounds/background.jpg
  194: OK "slick-greeter.conf written (top-right: battery + full date, 12h)"
  ```
  Verified: `xfce/background.jpg` does not exist at HEAD. Deleted in commit `0b970457` ("feat: split repo into xfce-setup/ + gnome-setup"). Fresh openSUSE XFCE install → greeter points at nonexistent `/usr/share/backgrounds/background.jpg` → blank/black login screen at next boot. Script says `[ok]`.
- Recommendation: Make 181 conditional on the same flag — track a `_WALLPAPER_OK` var in the 175 block, and only `tee` the greeter conf when set. Drop line 194's unconditional `OK`, gate it on the `tee` exit status. Either restore `background.jpg` under `xfce/` or repoint to a tracked wallpaper (`wallpapers/bg1.jpg` exists).

REVIEW-002 Unpinned remote script piped into a shell — `curl | sh` in both installers
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/gnome/setup.sh:82, /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/xfce/setup.sh:87
- Severity: HIGH
- Category: Security
- Finding: `curl -sS https://starship.rs/install.sh | sh -s -- -y`. No pin, no checksum, no TLS-content verification. Also `-sS` without `-f` means an HTTP error page is piped to `sh` instead of failing — so `OK "starship installed"` can print on a 404 body. Executes whatever the endpoint serves at run time.
- Recommendation: Download to a temp file with `curl -fsSL -o`, verify against a pinned SHA256, then `sh`. Minimum viable fix: add `-f` to curl and pin a version (`https://starship.rs/install.sh` with an explicit release tag) instead of tracking `main`.

REVIEW-003 Out-of-tree kernel module built from an unpinned GitHub clone, installed and loaded as root
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/xfce/setup.sh:381-391
- Severity: HIGH
- Category: Security
- Finding: Clones a third-party repo, builds it, copies the `.ko` into `/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/...`, `depmod`s, and `modprobe`s it. Ring-0 code from an unpinned remote branch, in a predictable world-writable `/tmp` path.
  ```
  383: && git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/frederik-h/acer-wmi-battery.git /tmp/acer-wmi-battery \
  387:     sudo cp /tmp/acer-wmi-battery/acer-wmi-battery.ko "$KDIR/"
  391: sudo modprobe acer-wmi-battery || WARN "modprobe failed — will load after reboot"
  ```
  Also: `git clone` into a fixed `/tmp` path fails on re-run (dir exists, no `--force`/cleanup before clone), and the `rm -rf` at 392 is only on the success path — leftovers persist after a failed build.
- Recommendation: Pin to a commit SHA (`git clone && git checkout <sha>`), clone into `$(mktemp -d)` instead of `/tmp/acer-wmi-battery`, add a `trap` for cleanup on all exit paths. Note in `fresh-install.md` that this installs an unsigned kernel module and let the user opt in.

REVIEW-004 `.bashrc` install guard keys on `alias fresh=`, so repo updates never land after the first run
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/gnome/setup.sh:88-95,112 and /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/xfce/setup.sh:93-100,121
- Severity: HIGH
- Category: Correctness
- Finding: The "idempotent" guard tests for a content marker instead of comparing content:

  88: if grep -q '^alias fresh=' "$HOME_DIR/.bashrc" 2>/dev/null; then
  89:     OK ".bashrc aliases already present"
  90: elif [ -f "$REPO/.bashrc" ]; then
  91:     cp -b "$REPO/.bashrc" "$HOME_DIR/.bashrc"

  First run appends `alias fresh=` (line 113). Second run matches line 88 → the `cp` is skipped forever. Every future edit to `gnome/.bashrc` is silently never installed. Second bug in the same block: the shipped file defines `rest`, not `fresh` (`.bashrc:135 alias rest='...' # distro-fresh-alias`), and the cleanup `sed` at 112 only matches `^alias fresh=` — it deletes the `rest` line via the `# distro-fresh-alias` comment match and replaces it with `fresh`, silently renaming a user-facing alias with no notice.
- Recommendation: Gate on a content hash of the repo file, not a marker string — e.g. compare `sha256sum "$REPO/.bashrc"` against a stamp line appended on install, or just always `cp -b`.   .bashrc:137:  alias code='sudo /usr/sbin/sysctl -w vm.swappiness=180 ...'
  gnome/setup.sh:123: "alias code='sudo /usr/sbin/sysctl -w vm.swappiness=200 ...'"
  gnome/setup.sh:228: printf "vm.swappiness=200\n..." | sudo tee /etc/sysctl.d/99-swappiness.conf
  xfce/setup.sh:219:  printf "vm.swappiness=180\n..." | sudo tee /etc/sysctl.d/99-swappiness.conf
  ```
  The GNOME installer actively rewrites the `.bashrc` line from 180 → 200 (its `sed` at 128 deletes then re-appends), so the shipped `.bashrc` is wrong for the one DE that installs it. Nothing reconciles the live alias value with the sysctl default — running GNOME then XFCE setup on the same box flips `/etc/sysctl.d/99-swappiness.conf` with no warning.
- Recommendation: Single source of truth. Pick one per DE, define it once as a variable at the top of each setup.sh, and generate both the sysctl conf and the alias from it. Remove the hand-written `game`/`code` aliases from the `.bashrc` — the installer owns them.

REVIEW-006 Hardcoded `/home/julry/.opencode/bin` prepended to PATH — directory does not exist on this machine
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/{cosmic,gnome,xfce}/.bashrc:123
- Severity: HIGH
- Category: Security
- Finding: `export PATH="/home/julry/.opencode/bin:$PATH"`. Verified: `/home/julry/.opencode/bin` does not exist. Every interactive shell on every user starts with a nonexistent directory at the **front** of PATH — and on any other account, a nonexistent `/home/julry/...` entry persists. A PATH-front directory that a different local user can create becomes a binary-hijack vector. The repo's own convention one line later (`:124 export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"`) is the correct form. Compounding: `cosmic/` has **no** `setup.sh`, so `cosmic/.bashrc` is never passed through the `sed` at `gnome/setup.sh:60` / `xfce/setup.sh:62` that rewrites `/home/julry` → `$HOME_DIR`.
- Recommendation: `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` everywhere — line 124 already does exactly this. Delete line 123 or make it `$HOME`-relative.

REVIEW-007 `A && B || C` reports copy failures as "missing directory"; 187MB icon tree re-copied every run
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/xfce/setup.sh:136-139
- Severity: HIGH
- Category: Correctness
- Finding: `|| WARN` binds to the whole `&&` chain, so a failing `cp` prints `"$REPO/.config missing — skipped"` — a lie that sends the user looking in the wrong place.
  ```
  136: [ -d "$REPO/.config" ] && cp -rb "$REPO/.config/." "$HOME_DIR/.config/" || WARN "$REPO/.config missing — skipped"
  137: [ -d "$REPO/.themes" ] && cp -rb "$REPO/.themes/." "$HOME_DIR/.themes/" || WARN "$REPO/.themes missing — skipped"
  138: [ -d "$REPO/.icons" ] && cp -rb "$REPO/.icons/." "$HOME_DIR/.icons/" || WARN "$REPO/.icons missing — skipped"
  ```
  Line 138 additionally copies the entire 187MB `xfce/.icons/` WhiteSur theme on **every** run, and `-b` writes a fresh `.icons/*~` backup each time — unbounded backup growth. No existence check on the destination beyond `-d`, so re-runs are not no-ops.
- Recommendation: Split into `if [ -d src ]; then cp ... || WARN "copy of X failed"; else WARN "X missing"; fi`. For `.icons`, either drop `-b` for bulk theme trees or skip when a sentinel file already matches.

REVIEW-008 Duplicated config in two places: shipped `.bashrc` and installer-injected `.bashrc` lines
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/gnome/.bashrc:130-137 vs /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/gnome/setup.sh:98-142; same at /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/xfce/setup.sh:103-128
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Category: Maintainability
- Finding: The repo `.bashrc` already ships everything the installer then re-injects: `eval "$(starship init bash)"` (.bashrc:130 / setup.sh:99), `NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=1536"` (.bashrc:132 / setup.sh:140), `alias game`/`alias code` (.bashrc:136-137 / setup.sh:123-132), and the distro alias (.bashrc:135 / setup.sh:107). Both files must be hand-edited in lockstep. Already drifted — see REVIEW-005. The installer's `grep`-before-append guards keep it from double-appending, which is the only reason this isn't worse.
- Recommendation: Delete the installer-side injection block (98-142 gnome / 103-128 xfce) and let the `.bashrc` be the single source. For the genuinely distro-specific `fresh` alias, keep it in the installer but have it append only the distro delta, with the shared body in the `.bashrc`.

REVIEW-009 No `set -e` / `pipefail`, and unconditional `exit 0` — failures are invisible to any caller
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/gnome/setup.sh:6,410 and /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/xfce/setup.sh:6,439
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Category: Testability
- Finding: Both scripts open with `set -u` only. That's an intentional choice given the `run_step`/`FAILED_STEPS` design — but it's undermined by the ending:
  ```
  gnome/setup.sh:390: if [ "${#FAILED_STEPS[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  gnome/setup.sh:391:     echo " FAILED  : ${FAILED_STEPS[*]}  (re-run script or do manually via setup.md)"
  gnome/setup.sh:410: exit 0
  ```
  `${FAILED_STEPS[*]}` (line 391) is unquoted array expansion — cosmetic here, but the real issue is `exit 0` regardless. A wrapper, CI job, or `set -e` parent shell sees success on a run where zram, dconf, packages, and drivers all failed.
- Recommendation: `exit1` when `${#FAILED_STEPS[@]} -gt 0`, `exit 0` otherwise. Quote line 391 as `"${FAILED_STEPS[*]}"`. Leave `set -e` off — the step-collector pattern is fine, but it must be reflected in the exit code.

REVIEW-010 File headers point at directory names that no longer exist
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/gnome/setup.sh:3-4 and /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/xfce/setup.sh:3-4
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Category: Maintainability

  ```

  gnome/setup.sh:4: # Full instructions: gnome-setup/setup.md
  xfce/setup.sh:3:  # Run from inside the cloned repo:  bash xfce-setup/setup.sh

REVIEW-011 Generated screen-dim script uses a predictable world-writable `/tmp` state file
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/xfce/setup.sh:149-168 (specifically :156, :153)
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Category: Security
- Finding: The generated `toggle-screen-dim.sh` keys its toggle state on a fixed, unowned path:
  ```
  156: STATE_FILE="/tmp/.screen_dim_toggle_state"
  159: if [ -f "$STATE_FILE" ]; then
  161:     rm -f "$STATE_FILE"
  164:     touch "$STATE_FILE"
  ```
  Any other local user can pre-create that path. The victim's first toggle then goes down the `else` branch (brightness 0.6) instead of resetting to 1.0, and `rm -f` fails silently on a file it doesn't own. Predictable name in world-writable `/tmp` is the textbook symlink/pre-create pattern. Second issue: `DISPLAY_NAME` at153 is unguarded — if no ` connected` line matches, `xrandr --output "" --brightness 1.0` fails with no message, because the script sends nothing to stderr suppression but has no error path at all.
- Recommendation: Use `STATE_FILE="${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/.screen_dim_toggle_state"` — `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is per-user `0700`. Guard line 153 with `[ -z "$DISPLAY_NAME" ] && { echo "no display found" >&2; exit 1; }`.

REVIEW-012 DKMS source copy is not idempotent — second run nests the directory and breaks the build
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/xfce/setup.sh:364-368
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Category: Correctness
- Finding: `cp -r src /usr/src/mt7902-wifi-1.0` copies **into** the destination when it already exists as a directory:
  ```
  364: && sudo cp -r "$REPO/drivers/mt7902/mt7902-wifi" /usr/src/mt7902-wifi-1.0 \
  365: && sudo cp -r "$REPO/drivers/mt7902/mt7902-bt" /usr/src/mt7902-bifi-1.0
  ```
  (line 365 is `mt7902-bt-1.0`.) A second run after a partial failure yields `/usr/src/mt7902-wifi-1.0/mt7902-wifi/…`, then `dkms install` and `make install_fw` fail. Every other step in this script advertises idempotency; this one isn't.
- Recommendation: `sudo rm -rf /usr/src/mt7902-{wifi,bt}-1.0` before the copies, or use `cp -rT` (GNU `--no-target-directory`) which replaces the destination atomically. Both exist on openSUSE.

REVIEW-013 Interactive zoxide selection is word-split before being passed to `zoxide`
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/{cosmic,gnome,xfce}/.bashrc:150
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Category: Correctness
- Finding: `target="$(zoxide query -i "${@:2}")"` passes the multi-word interactive selection unquoted, so a directory containing a space (e.g. `/home/julry/repo/my project`) is split into separate args, the query fails, and the `|| return 1` at the end of the line swallows it into a bare exit 1 with no message. The sibling call at 184 uses the same unquoted form: `zoxide query -i "$@"`.
- Recommendation: Quote both — `zoxide query -i "${@:2}"` and `zoxide query -i "$@"`.

REVIEW-014 `_launch_and_exit` discards all output and always reports success

- Severity: MEDIUM
- Category: Correctness
- Finding:
  ```
  142:  nohup zed "$target" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
  144:  exit 0
  ```
  If `zed` is not on PATH — and it is **not** installed by either setup script (`gnome/setup.sh:397` and `xfce/setup.sh:422` both list zed under "manual leftovers") — the launch fails, the error is thrown away by `2>&1` to `/dev/null`, and `exit 0` still reports success. The shell window just never opens an editor.
- Recommendation: Check `command -v zed` first and error out; capture the launch status instead of hardcoding `exit 0`. Drop `2>&1` so real failures surface in the terminal.

REVIEW-015 `fastfetch` runs on every shell opened in `$HOME`
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/{cosmic,gnome,xfce}/.bashrc:126-128
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Category: Performance
- Finding: `if [ "$PWD" = "$HOME" ]; then fastfetch; fi` blocks shell startup on every new terminal opened in the home dir, with no opt-out and no guard on the binary existing. Measurably slower `cd ~ && pty` round-trips.
- Recommendation: Guard with `command -v fastfetch`, or gate behind a flag var defaulting on that the user can set to off in `.bash_aliases`.

REVIEW-016 Path-rewrite `sed` mutates the git working tree and swallows its own errors
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/gnome/setup.sh:60-64 and /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/xfce/setup.sh:62-65
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Category: Maintainability
- Finding:
  ```
  60: sed -i "s|/home/julry|$HOME_DIR|g" \
  61:     "$REPO/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc" \
  62:     "$REPO/.bashrc" \
  63:     "$REPO/dconf/dash-to-panel.dconf" 2>/dev/null || true
  64: OK "paths rewritten"
  ```
  Three problems: (a) `2>/dev/null || true` hides GNU sed's "can't read file" errors, so line 64 prints `[ok] paths rewritten` even if every file was missing; (b) it rewrites files **inside the clone**, leaving `git status` permanently dirty and making the tree non-idempotent across runs (a second run is a no-op, a `git checkout` restores the old paths, a re-run re-dirties); (c) `cosmic/` is not in either list, so `cosmic/.bashrc` keeps `/home/julry` permanently (see REVIEW-006).
- Recommendation: Verify the replacement actually landed (`grep -q '/home/julry' file && WARN`) before printing `OK`. Better: stop shipping absolute paths — template them (`${HOME}` placeholders expanded at copy time) so no in-place mutation is needed. Add `cosmic/.bashrc` to the list if cosmic is supported.

REVIEW-017 Three byte-identical `.bashrc` copies; `cosmic/` has no installer at all
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/cosmic/.bashrc, /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/gnome/.bashrc, /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/xfce/.bashrc
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Category: Maintainability

That is the finding: three independent copies of one file with zero DE-specific differences, so every future edit must land in all three or the copies drift. The asymmetry that will cause drift is already visible in the installers — `gnome/setup.sh` and `xfce/setup.sh` mutate their local copy differently, and only two of the three have a `setup.sh` (`cosmic/` contains just `.config/` and `.bashrc`; no `setup.sh`, no `dconf/`, no `assets/`, and its `.config/` lacks `opencode/opencode.jsonc`).
- Recommendation: Keep one `.bashrc` at repo root; each DE dir symlinks or the setup scripts copy from it. Drop the per-DE copies and stop maintaining three. Either add a `cosmic/setup.sh` or document cosmic as config-only, explicitly.

REVIEW-018 `pkg_in()` defined in the GNOME installer and never called

- Severity: MEDIUM
- Category: Maintainability

REVIEW-019 No way to verify any of this without running it destructively
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles (repo-wide; no test or CI artifacts exist)
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Category: Testability
- Finding: No `.github/`, no Makefile, no `*.bats`, no test directory, no `shellcheck` installed on this machine (`command -v shellcheck` → not found). Every check in both setup scripts is destructive by construction: they write to `/etc/sysctl.d/`, `/etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf`, `/etc/sysconfig/earlyoom`, `/etc/lightdm/`, `/etc/modules-load.d/`, `/usr/src/`, `/lib/modules/`, and `/usr/share/backgrounds/`, and disable system services. The positive exception: the script does verify post-state for zram (`zramctl` at gnome:247 / xfce:243) and checks pre-state before most writes — that pattern is sound, it just isn't covered by anything automated.
- Recommendation: Lowest-cost win: add `shellcheck` with `-x` to a one-line `make lint` (it would flag SC2016, SC2086, and SC2120 in these files today). Next: wrap the `[ -f "$REPO/…" ]` guard paths in a `--dry-run` flag that skips every `sudo` and prints the intended command instead. No framework needed.

REVIEW-020 `zzed` dereferences `$1` before checking `$#`
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/{cosmic,gnome,xfce}/.bashrc:148,155
- Severity: LOW
- Category: Correctness
- Finding: `if [ "$1" = "-i" ]` at148 runs before `if [ $# -eq 0 ]` at 155. With no args `$1` expands empty and the test is simply false, so it works today — but any `set -u` inherited into an interactive subshell (`bash -u`, a strict CI wrapper sourcing this file) aborts on the unbound variable before the zero-arg branch is ever reached.
- Recommendation: Move the `[ $# -eq 0 ]` block above line 148.

REVIEW-021 `repo ref` silently does nothing when `~/repo` is absent
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/{cosmic,gnome,xfce}/.bashrc:194-200
- Severity: LOW
- Category: Correctness
- Finding: `for d in "$HOME/repo"/*/` — when the directory doesn't exist the glob stays literal, `[ -d "$d" ]` is false for every iteration, and the function returns 0 having done nothing. No diagnostic.
- Recommendation: `[ -d "$HOME/repo" ] || { echo "repo: $HOME/repo not found" >&2; return 1; }` before the loop.

REVIEW-022 `sudo` invoked inside a package-availability loop
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/gnome/setup.sh:70-73 and /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/xfce/setup.sh:72-75
- Severity: LOW
- Category: Performance
- Finding: `if sudo zypper se -x --match-exact "$_pkg"` runs once per package (8 iterations gnome, 12 xfce). Each is a full zypper refresh of repo metadata. Adds seconds and repeated credential checks for a purely informational dry-check.
- Recommendation: Query once and parse: `sudo zypper se -x 'fastfetch kitty ...' >/dev/null` in a single call, or run the whole loop through a single `sudo bash -c` to reuse one timestamp.

REVIEW-023 Multi-unit `systemctl disable --now` reports failure when any single unit is missing
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/gnome/setup.sh:325 and /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/xfce/setup.sh:325
- Severity: LOW
- Category: Correctness
- Finding: `sudo systemctl disable --now cups.service cups.socket avahi-daemon.service avahi-daemon.socket` returns non-zero if *any* named unit is absent. On a system without Avahi (common on openSUSE GNOME where it may already be removed), three units succeed and the script still emits `WARN "cups/avahi disable had failures — continuing"` plus a `FAILED_STEPS` entry. Misleading signal in the final summary.
- Recommendation: Iterate units individually and aggregate, or append `--` / filter to installed units first via `systemctl list-unit-files`.

REVIEW-024 `REPO` resolution breaks when the script is piped or sourced from stdin
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/gnome/setup.sh:8 and /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/xfce/setup.sh:8
- Severity: LOW
- Category: Portability
- Finding: `REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"` — under `set -u`, `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` is unset when the script is fed via `curl … | bash` or `bash < setup.sh`, aborting with an unbound-variable error. The headers do direct users to `bash gnome/setup.sh`, so this is an edge case, but it's an unhelpful one.
- Recommendation: `REPO="${REPO:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-$0}")" && pwd)}"`.

REVIEW-025 `systemctl restart` on a swap unit cannot re-create the device
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/gnome/setup.sh:246 and /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/xfce/setup.sh:242
- Severity: LOW
- Category: Correctness
- Finding: `sudo systemctl restart dev-zram0.swap` restarts the swap unit; it does not recreate `/dev/zram0` with new compression settings. The script's own verify step (`zramctl`) is what actually catches a no-op, which is why the `WARN "zram config written but zstd not active — reboot"` branch at gnome:250 exists — the outcome depends on the user noticing and rebooting.
- Recommendation: Drop the restart; the `systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service` enable plus the `zramctl` verification are sufficient, and say plainly in the message that a reboot is required.

Read-only review done. All files verified present. Findings below.

REVIEW-001 Autostart entry grants root permanent X11 access on every login
- File/Path: cosmic/.config/autostart/xhost-root.desktop:4
- Severity: CRITICAL
- Category: Security
- Finding: `Exec=xhost +si:localuser:root` in an autostart entry named "Allow Root GUI Apps". Grants root full X server access for the whole X session. Never revoked — nothing runs `xhost -SI:localuser:root`. Any local X client bug (image parsing, clipboard, fontconfig, browser render) becomes root. Access survives until X restart; `sudo` alone does not grant X, so root X access is otherwise unreachable for YaST GUI.
- Recommendation: Remove the autostart file. Run `xhost +SI:localuser:root` on demand in the same shell that launches the privileged GUI, and revoke in a trap: `xhost +SI:localuser:root; polkit-gnome …; xhost -SI:localuser:root`. If it must stay, add `Exec=sh -c 'xhost +si:localuser:root; …'` with a paired revoke and document the exposure.

REVIEW-002 Same root-X grant duplicated inside sway session start
- File/Path: sway/.config/sway/config:276
- Severity: HIGH
- Category: Security

REVIEW-009 All three fastfetch configs are group-writable (0664) — and are NOT root-owned
- File/Path: cosmic/.config/fastfetch/config.jsonc:1, gnome/.config/fastfetch/config.jsonc:1, xfce/.config/fastfetch/config.jsonc:1
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Category: Security
- Finding: Correcting the stated assumption: `stat` shows `-rw-rw-r-- julry:julry` on all three. No root-owned file exists in this repo. Real issue: mode 0664 while every other reviewed config is 0644, and git records mode `100644` (non-group-write), so the group-write bit is untracked local state that will silently vanish on re-clone — or, worse, be re-applied by a `chmod -R g+w` in some setup step. Any member of group `julry` can rewrite these files.
- Recommendation: `chmod 644` on all three, add `chmod -R a-w` or a umask guard in setup, and stop relying on untracked mode bits for security-relevant settings.

REVIEW-010 Lock-screen autostart leaves the session unlocked for 3s and passes no session ID
- File/Path: gnome/.config/autostart/lock-screen.desktop:5
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Category: Security
- Finding: `Exec=sh -c 'sleep 3; /usr/bin/loginctl lock-session'`. Three issues: (a) with autologin the desktop is interactively usable for 3s on every login — anything that grabs input or spawns in that window gets a live unlocked session; (b) `loginctl lock-session` takes `[ID…]` per `loginctl --help`; no session is named, so behavior depends on the caller's session resolution; (c) single-quote argument quoting is not what the desktop-entry spec mandates (spec requires double quotes), it only works because GIO parses with `g_shell_parse_argv`.
- Recommendation: Drop the sleep and lock directly (`Exec=/usr/bin/loginctl lock-session "$XDG_SESSION_ID"` — note desktop Exec has no shell expansion, so use a `sh -c "..."` with double quotes), or use GNOME's own screen-shield-delay instead of a sleep-then-lock hack.

REVIEW-017 `xfce/setup.sh` installs a 187MB icon theme via `cp -rb` with no disk precheck
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/xfce/setup.sh:138
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Category: Performance
- Finding: `cp -rb "$REPO/.icons/." "$HOME_DIR/.icons/"` copies 43,099 files / 187MB. `cp -b` means any pre-existing file is copied to `<name>~` first — on a machine that already has WhiteSur installed, this roughly doubles to ~374MB before `fc-cache -f`. Live `lsblk` shows 476.9G total with root on btrfs (`/dev/nvme0n1p5[/@/.snapshots/238/snapshot]`), so space isn't currently a problem, but the script makes no precheck and `fresh-install.md` promises `Nothing is deleted from your system` without noting a ~374MB write. This is the concrete operational cost of the missing root `.gitignore` decision (REVIEW-003) being undocumented anywhere.
- Recommendation: Add a precheck: compute `du -sm "$REPO/.icons"` and require free space ≥ 2× before copying, warn-and-skip if short. Document the 187MB icon cost in `xfce/fresh-install.md` §3 so users can pre-trim the theme.

REVIEW-018 `opencode.json` and `.opencode/workspace.json` are invalid strict JSON
- File/Path: /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/opencode.json:8, /home/julry/repo/linux-dotfiles/.opencode/workspace.json:9
- Severity: MEDIUM
- Category: Correctness
- Finding: Both files end with a trailing line comment `// c: worrie`. `python3 -c "json.load(...)"` → `JSONDecodeError: Extra data: line 8 column 1 (char 156)` and `line 9 column 1 (char 258)`. OpenCode itself tolerates JSONC in `opencode.json`, but: (a) `workspace.json` declares `"$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json"` and is read by the `-init`/`-obsidian`/`-archive` flag handlers described in `.clinerules`; any tooling that parses it with a strict JSON parser (jq, python, a CI schema check) fails. (b) The repo's own `xfce/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` is *doubly* invalid — `JSONDecodeError: Illegal trailing comma before end of object: line 7 column 33` — so the pattern is already inconsistent across the repo (`.jsonc` files do carry trailing commas, `.json` files don't).
- Recommendation: Remove the `// c: worrie` line from `opencode.json` and `.opencode/workspace.json`, or rename both to `.jsonc` and confirm every consumer tolerates JSONC. Add a repo-level check (`python3 -m json.tool` over the strict-JSON files) to CI.

REVIEW-020 `workspace.json` identity fields name a project that no longer exists

- Severity: MEDIUM

The repo directory is `linux-dotfiles`, the git remote is `.../linux-dotfiles.git`, and the README is titled `linux-dotfiles`. `.clinerules` §OBSIDIAN SYNC mandates `Use exact \`project_name\` (spaces preserved)` to build the vault mirror path, so `-obsidian` will mirror into `<vault>/linux-configs/` — a directory name that corresponds to nothing in the repo. # REPO REVIEW LEDGER — `worriee/linux-dotfiles`

Scope: `cosmic/ gnome/ sway/ xfce/ sessions/ README.md AGENTS.md opencode.json` + top-level configs. Excluded per your instruction: `.opencode/memory/`, `.opencode/rules/`, `.opencode/skills/`, `.opencode/node_modules/`, `xfce/.icons/` internals.

51 raw findings from 3 agents → 30 distinct after dedupe/merge.

## CRITICAL

```
R-001 Autostart grants root permanent X11 access, never revoked
- File/Path: cosmic/.config/autostart/xhost-root.desktop:4  +  sway/.config/sway/config:276
- Severity: CRITICAL
- Category: Security
- Finding: Two independent sites grant root full X server access for the whole session.
  cosmic/.config/autostart/xhost-root.desktop:4  ->  Exec=xhost +si:localuser:root
  sway/.config/sway/config:276                   ->  exec sh -c 'command -v xhost >/dev/null && xhost +SI:localuser:root'
  xhost IS installed (/usr/bin/xhost), so the sway guard passes and the grant fires.
  Nothing ever runs xhost -SI:localuser:root. Any local X client bug (image decode, clipboard,
  fontconfig, browser render) becomes root. Verified both lines byte-exact.
- Recommendation: Delete both sites. For YaST GUI, scope the grant to one command and revoke in a
  trap: xhost +SI:localuser:root; polkit-gnome …; xhost -SI:localuser:root
```

```
R-002 slick-greeter config written unconditionally to a wallpaper deleted from the repo, reports [ok]
- File/Path: xfce/setup.sh:175-194
- Severity: CRITICAL
- Category: Correctness
- Finding: Line 175 detects missing xfce/background.jpg and warns, but the config write at 181 runs
  unconditionally anyway, and line 194 prints OK unconditionally.
  181: sudo tee /etc/lightdm/slick-greeter.conf >/dev/null <<'EOF'
  183:   background=/usr/share/backgrounds/background.jpg
  194: OK "slick-greeter.conf written"
  Verified: xfce/background.jpg does NOT exist at HEAD (deleted in 0b970457). A fresh XFCE install
  greets the user with a black login screen and the script reports success.
- Recommendation: Gate the tee on the same flag that detected the wallpaper. Wallpapers/bg1.jpg is
  tracked in-repo — repoint to it, or drop the background= line entirely.
```

## HIGH

```
R-003 24 sk-shaped strings in committed transcripts will hard-fail secret scanning
- File/Path: sessions/session-oct-6.md, session-oct-6-1.md, session-oct-8.md, session-oct-10.md
- Severity: HIGH
- Category: Security
- Finding: I verified every match: mask-image / mask-composite / mask-origin SVG attribute dumps
  concatenated into sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}. FALSE POSITIVES — no credential exists. But the repo is
  public and the shape is byte-identical to a live OpenAI key, so GitHub push protection and any
  scanner will reject pushes.
- Recommendation: .gitattributes with sessions/* -diff, plus sessions/ out of git entirely (see R-014).
```

```
R-004 .bashrc install guard blocks every future repo update, and a sed silently renames the shipped alias
- File/Path: gnome/setup.sh:88-95,112  +  xfce/setup.sh:93-100,121
- Severity: HIGH
- Category: Correctness
- Finding: The "idempotent" guard tests for a marker string, not content:
  88: if grep -q '^alias fresh=' "$HOME_DIR/.bashrc"; then OK ".bashrc aliases already present"
  First run appends the marker; every later run skips the cp forever. Edit gnome/.bashrc, rerun the
  installer, nothing lands — silently. Second bug same block: the shipped .bashrc defines `rest`
  (.bashrc:135, tagged # distro-fresh-alias), and the cleanup sed only matches ^alias fresh=, so it
  deletes the `rest` line and re-adds it as `fresh` — a user-facing rename with no notice.
- Recommendation: Gate on sha256 of the repo file, not a marker. Never sed-delete user aliases.
```

```
R-005 Unpinned remote script piped into a shell, no -f on curl
- File/Path: gnome/setup.sh:82  +  xfce/setup.sh:87
- Severity: HIGH
- Category: Security
- Finding: curl -sS https://starship.rs/install.sh | sh -s -- -y — no pin, no checksum. Worse, -sS
  without -f means an HTTP 404 body is piped into sh, and the script still prints OK.
- Recommendation: curl -fsSL -o to a temp file, verify SHA256 against a pinned release, then sh.
```

```
R-006 Unpinned third-party kernel module built and modprobed as root from a fixed /tmp path
- File/Path: xfce/setup.sh:381-392
- Severity: HIGH
- Category: Security
- Finding: git clone --depth=1 (unpinned branch) -> make -> cp .ko into /lib/modules/$(uname -r) ->
  depmod -> sudo modprobe. Ring-0 code from a moving remote ref, into a predictable world-writable
  /tmp path. Re-run fails (dir exists, no cleanup before clone). The rm -rf is success-path only.
- Recommendation: Clone to $(mktemp -d), pin a commit SHA, trap cleanup on all exits.
```

```
R-007 Nonexistent directory prepended to PATH, permanently
- File/Path: {cosmic,gnome,xfce}/.bashrc:123
- Severity: HIGH
- Category: Security
- Finding: export PATH="/home/julry/.opencode/bin:$PATH" — verified that directory does not exist.
  Every interactive shell starts with a nonexistent dir at the FRONT of PATH. On any account, a
  /home/julry/.opencode/bin that any user can create becomes a binary-hijack vector. Line 124 of the
  same file already does it correctly with $HOME/.local/bin.
- Recommendation: Delete line 123. cosmic/.bashrc is also absent from both installers' sed rewrite
  lists (gnome:60, xfce:62), so it keeps the hardcoded /home/julry forever.
```

```
R-008 Swappiness contradicts itself across .bashrc, both installers, and both docs
- File/Path: {cosmic,gnome,xfce}/.bashrc:137 | gnome/setup.sh:123,228 | xfce/setup.sh:219

- Severity: HIGH
- Category: Maintainability
- Finding: Four different claims for one knob. .bashrc:137 sets 180. gnome/setup.sh rewrites that
  exact line 180 -> 200 and writes 200 to /etc/sysctl.d. xfce/setup.sh:219 writes 180.
  gnome/setup.md:404 says "swappiness 180" in a section that documents the 200 setup.
  README.md implies GNOME shares XFCE's 180. Live value is 200.
- Recommendation: One variable per installer, generate both the sysctl drop-in and the alias from it.
  Remove the hand-written aliases from .bashrc — the installer owns that knob.
```

```
R-009 `A && B || C` reports copy failure as "missing directory"; recopies 187MB every run
- File/Path: xfce/setup.sh:136-139
- Severity: HIGH
- Category: Correctness
- Finding: [ -d src ] && cp -rb src/. dest/ || WARN "src missing" — the || binds to the whole && chain,
  so a failed cp prints "missing", sending the user to the wrong place. Line 138 copies the entire
  43,099-file / 187MB icon theme on EVERY run, and -b writes a fresh .icons/*~ backup each time —
  unbounded growth, no destination check, not a no-op.
- Recommendation: if/else instead of && ||. Skip the theme copy when a sentinel file already matches.
```

```
R-010 Idle lock is entirely commented out while config prose and README both promise a 900s lock
- File/Path: sway/.config/sway/config:46-51  +  sway/README.md:13-14
- Severity: HIGH
- Category: Security
- Finding: Lines 46-48 are dead comments. The prose directly below them reads "Locks after 900s
  (15min) idle" and the README lists "idle lock 900s". No idle daemon starts. An unattended session
  stays unlocked indefinitely, and the docs actively claim otherwise.
- Recommendation: Uncomment the swayidle block, or delete the claim from both places.
```

```
R-011 WiFi passphrase passed as an nmcli argv, visible to every local user
- File/Path: sway/.local/bin/wifi-menu.sh:24-25
- Severity: HIGH
- Category: Security
- Finding: nmcli device wifi connect "$SSID" password "$PASS" — the PSK lands in /proc/<pid>/cmdline
  and in ps output for the lifetime of the call.
- Recommendation: nmcli --ask device wifi connect "$SSID" and drop the PASS capture entirely.
```

```
R-012 opencode compaction block uses four keys the live schema rejects
- File/Path: gnome/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc:4-7
- Severity: HIGH
- Category: Correctness

  compaction object allows only auto, prune, tail_turns, preserve_recent_tokens, reserved, with
  additionalProperties: false. All four are rejected. Verified content matches exactly.
  (The trailing comma after preserveSystemPrompt also makes it invalid strict JSON.)
- Recommendation: "compaction": { "auto": true, "prune": true, "tail_turns": 10, "reserved": 20000 }

Any other local user can pre-create it, forcing the victim's first toggle into the wrong brightness branch; `rm -f` then fails silently on a file it does not own. `DISPLAY_NAME` at line 153 is also unguarded — no match produces `xrandr --output \"\"` with no error path.\n- **Recommendation**: `STATE_FILE=\"${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/.screen_dim_toggle_state\"`; guard line 153 with an explicit exit 1.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-047] DKMS source copy is not idempotent — second run nests the directory (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `xfce/setup.sh:364-368`\n- **The Issue**: `cp -r \"$REPO/drivers/mt7902/mt7902-wifi\" /usr/src/mt7902-wifi-1.0` copies INTO the destination when it already exists, yielding `/usr/src/mt7902-wifi-1.0/mt7902-wifi/…`; `dkms install` and `make install_fw` then fail. Every other step in this script advertises idempotency — this one is not.\n- **Recommendation**: `sudo rm -rf` the destinations first, or use `cp -rT`. Both exist on openSUSE.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-048] `exit 0` returned even when every step failed (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Testability\n- **File/Path**: `gnome/setup.sh:390-410`, `xfce/setup.sh:~420-439`\n- **The Issue**: Both scripts end `exit 0` regardless of `${#FAILED_STEPS[@]}`. A CI job, wrapper, or `set -e` parent sees success on a run where zram, dconf, packages, and drivers all failed. `${FAILED_STEPS[*]}` at line 391 is also unquoted.\n- **Recommendation**: `exit 1` when failures exist, `exit 0` otherwise; quote the expansion. Leave `set -e` off — the step-collector pattern is sound, but the exit code must reflect it.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-049] Path-rewrite `sed` mutates the git clone and swallows its own errors (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Maintainability\n- **File/Path**: `gnome/setup.sh:60-64`, `xfce/setup.sh:62-65`\n- **The Issue**: `sed -i \"s|/home/julry|$HOME_DIR|g\" … 2>/dev/null || true` followed by `OK \"paths rewritten\"`. `2>/dev/null || true` hides every \"can't read file\" error, so the OK prints even when all three targets are missing. It rewrites files INSIDE the clone, leaving `git status` permanently dirty and non-idempotent across checkouts. `cosmic/.bashrc` is missing from the list (see REVIEW-033).\n- **Recommendation**: Verify the replacement landed before printing `OK`. Better — ship `${HOME}` placeholders expanded at copy time so no in-place mutation is needed.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-050] Three byte-identical `.bashrc` copies maintained independently (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Maintainability\n- **File/Path**: `cosmic/.bashrc`, `gnome/.bashrc`, `xfce/.bashrc`\n- **The Issue**: All three are git blob `6e6f15cc` — byte-identical, zero divergence. Three independent copies of one file with no DE-specific differences, so every future edit must land three times. `cosmic/` has no `setup.sh` at all, no `dconf/`, no `assets/`, and its `.config/` lacks `opencode/opencode.jsonc`.\n- **Recommendation**: One `.bashrc` at repo root; each DE dir symlinks or copies from it. Either add `cosmic/setup.sh` or document `cosmic/` as config-only.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-051] Three byte-identical `fastfetch` configs, no drift check (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Maintainability\n- **File/Path**: `cosmic/.config/fastfetch/config.jsonc`, `gnome/.config/fastfetch/config.jsonc`, `xfce/.config/fastfetch/config.jsonc`\n- **The Issue**: All three are git blob `2bd2cf39`, identical 2688 bytes, all mode `0664`. Any edit must be applied three times by hand with no mechanism to catch a miss. Demonstrated live on October 11, 2026 — the `os age` change had to be applied three times, and one copy silently failed on a root-owned permission error until caught.\n- **Recommendation**: One canonical file plus symlinks.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-052] Two byte-identical 21KB spotatui playlist manifests (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Maintainability\n- **File/Path**: `cosmic/.config/spotatui/youtube_playlists.yml`, `gnome/.config/spotatui/youtube_playlists.yml`\n- **The Issue**: 21,190 bytes each, identical, one playlist with 161 tracks. Regenerating rewrites 21KB twice.\n- **Recommendation**: One canonical file plus symlink, or generate per-session copies from a single source during setup.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-053] 20+ hardcoded `/home/julry/...` absolute paths across configs and scripts (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Portability\n- **File/Path**: 3× `fastfetch/config.jsonc:5`, `sway/.config/sway/config:19,34,177,236,237,240,263`, `sway/.config/waybar/config:50,60,65,70`, `sway/.local/bin/shot.sh:4`, `sway/.local/bin/notif-center.sh:25`, `sway/.local/bin/power-menu.sh:11`\n- **The Issue**: The fastfetch logo points at `/home/julry/Documents/jm-icon.png`, outside the repo entirely. Sway alone carries 14 absolute references. A restore-as-documented leaves every one of them dangling for any other user or machine.\n- **Recommendation**: `~` or `$HOME` throughout; vendor the logo inside the repo so the copies stay self-contained.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-054] Starship prompt hardcodes the username `julry` (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `gnome/.config/starship.toml:5`\n- **The Issue**: `[ julry](bg:#a3aed2 fg:#090c0c)` is a literal string in `format`. Every other user of this repo gets a prompt that lies about who they are.\n- **Recommendation**: Replace the literal with starship's `$username` module, styled identically.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-055] Repo copies have drifted from the live home configs they mirror (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Maintainability\n- **File/Path**: `gnome/.config/zed/settings.json:131`, `gnome/.config/kitty/kitty.conf:6`\n- **The Issue**: Repo has `\"dark\": \"Transparent Prism - Sunset\"`, live has `\"dark\": \"Ayu Glass Dark\"`. Repo has `font_size 10.0`, live has `11.0`. `starship.toml` and `zed/keymap.json` are identical. The repo claims to be the source of truth; restoring it would revert two live settings the user changed since.\n- **Recommendation**: Sync repo from live, or date-stamp the snapshot and mark those two files non-authoritative.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-056] `xfce/setup.md` is Linux Mint/apt-only prose on an openSUSE repo (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `xfce/setup.md` (28 apt references; §1A:39, §1E:188, §4F:529, §11:1012)\n- **The Issue**: Every step after §0 is apt-only. `apt`, `dpkg`, `tune2fs`, `update-grub`, `update-alternatives`, `xrandr`, `xfconf-query` are all absent on the live box. §1A tells the reader to edit `/etc/sysctl.conf` while `xfce/setup.sh:219` writes a `/etc/sysctl.d/99-swappiness.conf` drop-in — different mechanism, different file, never mentioned.\n- **Recommendation**: Two-column Mint-vs-openSUSE, or an explicit banner at §0. Fix §1A to document the drop-in the script actually writes.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-057] `xfce/setup.md` claims the Acer battery driver is loaded when it is not (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `xfce/setup.md:318`\n- **The Issue**: Claims \"driver is installed and loading at boot\". Verified: `lsmod` shows only `acer_wmi`, `acer_wireless`, `wmi-bmof` — no `acer-wmi-battery`, and `/sys/bus/wmi/drivers/` contains only `wmi-bmof`. Every `batt80`/`batt100`/`battstat` alias in §2B fails. `gnome/setup.md:164` correctly states the opposite — the two docs disagree about the same hardware and the XFCE one is wrong.\n- **Recommendation**: Correct line 318 to match reality and align with `gnome/setup.md:164`.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-058] MT7902 DKMS presented as live procedure while the doc itself calls it deprecated (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `xfce/setup.md:240-310`, `:1094`, `xfce/setup.sh:357-374`\n- **The Issue**: §2A is written as an active 6-step install; the deprecation note sits at line 300 and the summary table at line 1094 claims \"Wi-Fi + BT work on MediaTek 7902 cards\". Verified: `lsmod` shows in-kernel `mt7921e` active; `mt7902e`/`btusb_mt7902` are not loaded. Line 244 claims \"no in-kernel driver on Mint 22.3\", contradicted by line 246 in the same section. `xfce/setup.sh` still attempts the DKMS install and `dkms` is not installed on this box; its guard checks `dkms status` but not whether the in-kernel driver is already loaded, unlike `gnome/setup.sh:360`.\n- **Recommendation**: Lead with `DEPRECATED`, match `gnome/setup.md`'s treatment, fix the summary row, and guard on `lsmod | grep mt7921e`.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-059] `opencode.json` and `workspace.json` are invalid strict JSON (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `opencode.json:8`, `.opencode/workspace.json:9`, `xfce/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc:7`\n- **The Issue**: Both root files end with a trailing `// c: worrie` comment; `python3 -m json.tool` fails with `Extra data`. `workspace.json` declares the opencode schema and is read by the `-init`/`-obsidian`/`-archive` handlers, so any strict-JSON tooling (jq, CI) breaks. The repo's own `.jsonc` is doubly invalid — trailing comma after `preserveSystemPrompt`.\n- **Recommendation**: Drop the comment line from both `.json` files, or rename to `.jsonc` and confirm every consumer tolerates JSONC.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-060] `workspace.json` identity fields name a project that no longer exists (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Maintainability\n- **File/Path**: `.opencode/workspace.json:3-4`\n- **The Issue**: `workspace_id` and `project_name` are both `linux-configs`, but the repo directory, git remote, and README all say `linux-dotfiles`. `.clinerules` §OBSIDIAN SYNC mandates using the exact `project_name` to build the vault mirror path, so `-obsidian` will mirror into `<vault>/linux-configs/` — a directory corresponding to nothing in the repo.\n- **Recommendation**: Requires explicit user authorization — `.clinerules` forbids editing identity fields after init. Change both to `linux-dotfiles` and note the rationale in `project_memory.md`.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-061] `AGENTS.md` omits `project_memory.md` and `.opencode/archives/` (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Maintainability\n- **File/Path**: `AGENTS.md:23-28`\n- **The Issue**: The \"Memory File Locations\" section lists `rules/` and `memory/` but never mentions `project_memory.md` — which lives in `rules/`, not `memory/`, despite being load-bearing for three flags (`-init`, `-obsidian`, `-archive`) — nor `.opencode/archives/`, which exists with 5 files and is the defined archival target.\n- **Recommendation**: Add both entries to the memory section. All 13 paths AGENTS.md does list exist — no dead paths there.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-062] Lock-screen autostart leaves the session unlocked for 3s and passes no session ID (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Security\n- **File/Path**: `gnome/.config/autostart/lock-screen.desktop:5`\n- **The Issue**: `Exec=sh -c 'sleep 3; /usr/bin/loginctl lock-session'`. Three problems — a 3-second interactively-usable window on every login (fatal under autologin), `loginctl lock-session` takes `[ID…]` and none is named so resolution depends on the caller, and single-quote quoting is not what the desktop-entry spec mandates (it only works because GIO uses `g_shell_parse_argv`).\n- **Recommendation**: Lock directly with `\"$XDG_SESSION_ID\"`, or use GNOME's own screen-shield-delay instead of sleep-then-lock.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-063] fastfetch configs are group-writable while git records 0644 (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Security\n- **File/Path**: 3× `fastfetch/config.jsonc`\n- **The Issue**: `-rw-rw-r-- julry:jully` on all three, while git records mode `100644`. The group-write bit is untracked local state that vanishes silently on re-clone, or gets re-applied by a stray `chmod -R g+w`. Any member of group `julry` can rewrite these files.\n- **Recommendation**: `chmod 644`; add a umask guard in setup; do not rely on untracked mode bits for security-relevant settings.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-064] Secure Boot section pins three different stale kernel versions as \"verified live\" (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `gnome/setup.md:158,475,639,659`\n- **The Issue**: Claims verified live state with `kernel-default` 7.2.5-1.1 + 7.2.6-1.1; line 158 says 7.2.4; line 639 gives `sudo kernel-install remove 7.2.5-1-default` for a version no longer installed; line 659 says keep 7.2.5 as fallback. Live running kernel is `7.2.9-1-default`. The \"verified live\" framing lends false authority to stale values.\n- **Recommendation**: Replace pinned versions with `uname -r` derivation; add a `Last verified:` marker.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-065] Waybar exposes 5 workspaces while sway binds 10 (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `sway/.config/waybar/config:11` vs `sway/.config/sway/config:125-145`\n- **The Issue**: `persistent-workspaces` maps 1–5; sway binds 1–10; `disable-scroll: true` removes the scroll fallback. Workspaces 6–10 exist but are unreachable from the bar.\n- **Recommendation**: Extend the map to 10, or drop the sway bindings for 6–10.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-066] `zoxide query -i` receives an unquoted multi-word selection (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `{cosmic,gnome,xfce}/.bashrc:150,184`\n- **The Issue**: `zoxide query -i \"${@:2}\"` and `zoxide query -i \"$@\"` split on spaces, so a directory like `/home/julry/repo/my project` fails; the `|| return 1` swallows it into a bare exit 1 with no message.\n- **Recommendation**: Quote both.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-067] `_launch_and_exit` discards all output and always reports success (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `{cosmic,gnome,xfce}/.bashrc:140-145`\n- **The Issue**: `nohup zed \"$target\" >/dev/null 2>&1 &` then a hardcoded `exit 0`. `zed` is not installed by either setup script — both list it under \"manual leftovers\" — so the launch fails, the error is thrown away, and success is still reported. The editor simply never opens.\n- **Recommendation**: `command -v zed` guard; drop `2>&1`; capture the real status.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-068] `fastfetch` runs on every shell opened in `$HOME` (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Performance\n- **File/Path**: `{cosmic,gnome,xfce}/.bashrc:126-128`\n- **The Issue**: `if [ \"$PWD\" = \"$HOME\" ]; then fastfetch; fi` blocks shell startup with no guard on the binary existing and no opt-out.\n- **Recommendation**: `command -v fastfetch` guard, or gate behind a flag var.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-069] `zzed` dereferences `$1` before checking `$#` (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `{cosmic,gnome,xfce}/.bashrc:148,155`\n- **The Issue**: `if [ \"$1\" = \"-i\" ]` runs before `if [ $# -eq 0 ]`. Works today because `$1` expands empty, but aborts under an inherited `set -u` before the zero-arg branch is reached.\n- **Recommendation**: Move the `[ $# -eq 0 ]` block above line 148.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-070] `repo ref` silently no-ops when `~/repo` is absent (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `{cosmic,gnome,xfce}/.bashrc:194-200`\n- **The Issue**: `for d in \"$HOME/repo\"/*/` — the glob stays literal when the directory is missing, `[ -d \"$d\" ]` is false for every iteration, and the function returns 0 having done nothing. No diagnostic.\n- **Recommendation**: `[ -d \"$HOME/repo\" ] || { echo \"repo: not found\" >&2; return 1; }` before the loop.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-071] `pkg_in()` defined and never called (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Maintainability\n- **File/Path**: `gnome/setup.sh:45-47`\n- **The Issue**: The only call sites are in `xfce/setup.sh` (306, 362, 363, 381, 382). GNOME installs packages via an inline `bash -c` string at line 75 instead — dead code plus a second divergent install path.\n- **Recommendation**: Delete it, or route line 75 through `pkg_in`.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-072] `sudo zypper se` inside a per-package loop (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Performance\n- **File/Path**: `gnome/setup.sh:70-73`, `xfce/setup.sh:72-75`\n- **The Issue**: `sudo zypper se -x --match-exact \"$_pkg\"` runs once per package — 8 and 12 full repo-metadata refreshes plus repeated credential checks, for a purely informational dry-check.\n- **Recommendation**: One `zypper se` call for the whole list, or a single `sudo bash -c`.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-073] Multi-unit `systemctl disable --now` reports failure when any unit is missing (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `gnome/setup.sh:325`, `xfce/setup.sh:325`\n- **The Issue**: `systemctl disable --now cups.service cups.socket avahi-daemon.service avahi-daemon.socket` returns non-zero if ANY named unit is absent. On a system without Avahi, three units succeed and the script still emits a `WARN` plus a `FAILED_STEPS` entry — a misleading signal in the summary.\n- **Recommendation**: Iterate units individually and aggregate, or filter to installed units first.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-074] `REPO` resolution breaks when the script is piped or sourced from stdin (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Portability\n- **File/Path**: `gnome/setup.sh:8`, `xfce/setup.sh:8`\n- **The Issue**: `REPO=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")\" && pwd)\"` — under `set -u`, `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` is unset when fed via `curl … | bash` or `bash < setup.sh`, aborting with an unbound-variable error.\n- **Recommendation**: `\"${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-$0}\"`.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-075] `systemctl restart` on a swap unit cannot recreate the device (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `gnome/setup.sh:246`, `xfce/setup.sh:242`\n- **The Issue**: `systemctl restart dev-zram0.swap` restarts the unit but does not recreate `/dev/zram0` with new compression settings. The outcome depends on the user noticing the WARN and rebooting.\n- **Recommendation**: Drop the restart; the generator enable plus `zramctl` verification suffice. Say plainly that a reboot is required.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-076] JSON config files carry the executable bit (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Maintainability\n- **File/Path**: `gnome/.config/zed/keymap.json` (0755), `gnome/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (0755)\n- **The Issue**: `-rwxr-xr-x` on JSON configs while sibling `settings.json` is 0644; git records `keymap.json` as `100755`. No functional impact, but it hides the real mode problem in REVIEW-063 from diffs.\n- **Recommendation**: `chmod 644`; `git update-index --chmod=-x` for `keymap.json`.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-077] sway includes a config directory that does not exist (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `sway/.config/sway/config:258`\n- **The Issue**: `include /etc/sway/config.d/*` — `/etc/sway` exists, `/etc/sway/config.d` does not. The glob matches nothing and sway logs an include failure on every config load.\n- **Recommendation**: `mkdir -p` on install, guard the include, or delete the line.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-078] Waybar backlight pinned to one GPU's device name (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `sway/.config/waybar/config:31`\n- **The Issue**: `\"device\": \"amdgpu_bl1\"` — a single-machine assumption; on any other GPU the module shows nothing.\n- **Recommendation**: Remove the key so waybar picks the first backlight, or comment it as hardware-specific.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-079] Waybar bluetooth reports OFF in every powered state (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `sway/.config/waybar/config:53-57`\n- **The Issue**: `format`, `format-disabled`, `format-off`, `format-on`, `format-no-controller` are all `\" OFF\"` — only `format-connected` differs, so a powered-but-not-connected radio reads OFF.\n- **Recommendation**: Give `format-on` a real string, or delete the redundant formats.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-080] fastfetch key padding inconsistency and desktop-only battery module (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: 3× `fastfetch/config.jsonc:107,112`\n- **The Issue**: Every other key is space-padded to 8 columns; `\"key\": \"packages\"` is not. The `battery` module renders nothing on a desktop.\n- **Recommendation**: Pad to `\"packages \"`; move `battery` into a laptop-only profile.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-081] spotatui commits a playlist ID and the full 161-track manifest (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Security\n- **File/Path**: `cosmic/.config/spotatui/youtube_playlists.yml:2`, `gnome/.config/spotatui/youtube_playlists.yml:2`\n- **The Issue**: Playlist ID `2npedfnskpte` plus every track title, channel, and duration. A public playlist ID is not a credential — but if the source playlist is unlisted, that ID is the only access control and it is now in git history. **No tokens or keys found anywhere in the repo (full secret scan clean).**\n- **Recommendation**: Drop the `id` field from the committed copy if the playlist is unlisted, or keep the file out of git.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-082] kitty.conf documents a compositor that is not installed (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `gnome/.config/kitty/kitty.conf:15-16`\n- **The Issue**: The comment `# Frosted glass transparency for picom` sits above `background_opacity 0.85`. `picom` is not installed; kitty does this natively. The comment misattributes the effect and will mislead whoever adds a compositor later.\n- **Recommendation**: Reword to `# Transparency (kitty-native, no compositor needed)`.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-083] sway README points at a wallpaper that is now in the repo (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `sway/README.md:59`\n- **The Issue**: Says the wallpaper is \"not in repo\" — `wallpapers/bg1.jpg` is now tracked (4.3MB). The live copy at `/home/julry/wallpapers/bg1.jpg` also exists, giving two copies with no statement of which is authoritative.\n- **Recommendation**: Reference the tracked `wallpapers/bg1.jpg` and state which copy is canonical.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-084] Setup docs append to `.bashrc` non-idempotently, contradicting their own scripts (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `gnome/setup.md:143`, `xfce/setup.md:226`\n- **The Issue**: Both docs instruct `echo 'export NODE_OPTIONS=\"--max-old-space-size=1536\"' >> ~/.bashrc` unconditionally. **Verified root cause — the export shape, read straight off disk:**

| package | `dist/index.js` default export | v2 verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `opencode-caveman@0.1.4` | `{ id: "opencode-caveman", server: CavemanPlugin }` | **V1 API — rejected** |
| `@dietrichgebert/ponytail@5.1.0` | `{ id: 'ponytail', async setup(ctx) {…} }` | V2 API — accepted |

Ponytail's own source comment says it: *"One default export serves both plugin APIs: V2 reads `id` + `setup`, V1 calls `server()`."*

**UPSTREAM CHANGES 2.0.26 — CONFIRMED BREAKING CHANGE, not guessed.**
https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/migrate-v1 — verbatim warning: *"V1 plugin implementations do not run in V2. Moving a file or renaming its config entry is not enough."* V2 requires a default export `{ id, effect }` or `{ id, setup(ctx) }`. Same error text reproduced by other projects hitting this exact break (rtk-ai/rtk#4311, stablyai/orca#20407, code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent#9107).

**Config key rename is NOT your problem.** Docs say rename `plugin`→`plugins`, but empirically ponytail still loads from the singular `plugin` key on 2.0.26, and the published schema (https://opencode.ai/config.json) still exposes `plugin`. V2 normalizes it. Don't chase this.

**CORRECT CURRENT PLUGIN SPEC:**
- caveman: `"opencode-caveman"` is correct **as a spec string** — but npm `latest` is still `0.1.4`, published **2026-04-13**, and it is a V1 plugin. **No v2-compatible release exists.** Bumping will not fix it.
- ponytail: `"@dietrichgebert/ponytail"` correct. npm latest `5.1.0`, published 2026-10-08, dual-API, working.

```
ROOT CAUSE (most likely):
opencode-caveman@0.1.4 is a V1 plugin: its default export is { id, server }. OpenCode 2.0.26's
loader hard-validates the default export and requires `effect` or `setup`; the V1 `server` shape
is rejected with PluginModule.LoadError. The load fails at module-validation time, so the plugin
never enters the active plugin registry — hence no "caveman" in /plugins. The plugin is NOT
misconfigured, not cached wrong, not ownership-broken: ponytail 5.1.0 sits in the same config
array, same cache, same directory and loads fine because its default export has `setup(ctx)`.
This is upstream breakage: caveman 0.1.4 is 6 months stale and predates the v2 API.

SECONDARY FACT (why it's now completely absent from /plugins): at 2026-10-11 16:43:53 the LIVE
config was rewritten and "opencode-caveman" was deleted from the plugin array — the repo's gnome
copy still has it. So today it's doubly gone: broken code AND no longer configured.

CANDIDATE CAUSES RANKED:
  1. V1→V2 plugin API break, caveman 0.1.4 exports { id, server }. Evidence: exact log
     WARN with `Missing key at ["default"]["setup"]`; on-disk default export; official
     migrate-v1 doc; ponytail (`setup`) loads, caveman (`server`) fails, same cache dir.
  2. `opencode-caveman` was removed from the live config at 16:43:53 today. Evidence: mtime on
     ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc, array now holds ponytail only, repo copy still lists
     caveman. Real, but it masks cause #1 — restoring the line alone will NOT fix it.
  3. Config key renamed plugin→plugins. Evidence: doc says so — but REFUTED locally. Ponytail
     loads fine from `plugin`, and /opencode.ai/config.json still publishes `plugin`.

SUGGESTED FIX (DO NOT APPLY — for the user to run themselves):
  There is no upgrade that fixes this. The package has no v2 build. Options, cheapest first:
  a) Write a local V2 plugin at ~/.config/opencode/plugins/caveman.ts (that dir is auto-loaded —
     proven by rtk.ts loading). Port the three V1 hooks per the migration table:
       - V1 `config` (register skills path + /caveman commands) → `ctx.skill.transform` +
         `ctx.command.transform`
       - V1 `experimental.chat.messages.transform` → `ctx.session.hook("context", e => …)`
       - V1 `tool` map → `ctx.tool.transform`
     Then REMOVE "opencode-caveman" from the plugin array (a V2 local plugin and a broken package
     entry can coexist, but the broken entry only spams warnings).
     Cheapest real variant: caveman's whole value is prepending ~30 lines of terse-output rules,

  c) Do nothing to config; just accept the plugin is dead until 0.2.0 ships.
  Also worth doing separately: reinstall the dotfiles repo copy of the config, or the live
  config will keep drifting from gnome/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc.

README.md
opencode-caveman
npm
opencode-caveman is an OpenCode plugin that activates caveman token-compression automatically on every session. Terse responses. Full technical accuracy.
Get started
1. Install opencode-caveman:
  Project-level:
  opencode plugin opencode-caveman
  Global:
  opencode plugin -g opencode-caveman
2. Navigate to your project directory and run opencode .
  Caveman is active from the next session. No config required.
Commands
* Command | Description
* /caveman [lite | full | ultra | wenyan-lite | wenyan-full | wenyan-ultra] | Set compression level
* /caveman-commit | Terse commit message for staged changes
* /caveman-review | Terse code review of current diff
Skill
Load caveman instructions on demand:
use skill caveman
Levels
* Level | Style
* lite | No filler, full sentences
* full (default) | Fragments, no articles
* ultra | Abbreviations, arrows for causality
* wenyan-lite | Semi-classical Chinese register
* wenyan-full | Classical Chinese (文言文)
* wenyan-ultra | Extreme compression, classical feel
Uninstall
Remove opencode-caveman from your opencode.json plugin list, then:
npm uninstall opencode-caveman
Reporting Bugs
Use the /bug command to report issues directly within OpenCode, or file a GitHub issue .
Troubleshooting
If your OpenCode config is not at ~/.config/opencode , set OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR to the correct path before starting OpenCode. The plugin reads this env var to know where to install its files.

## [caveman-opencode-plugin](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/caveman-opencode-plugin@0.1.5/README.md)

caveman-opencode-plugin
Caveman communication mode plugin for opencode. Adapts JuliusBrussee/caveman into hook-based plugin.
Installation
Global install
opencode plugin caveman-opencode-plugin@latest --global
Or local install
opencode plugin caveman-opencode-plugin@latest
NPM: https://www.npmjs.com/package/caveman-opencode-plugin
Add to opencode.json:
{
"plugin": ["caveman-opencode-plugin"]
}
Setup
Run the interactive setup script:
Download and run
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dantesCode/caveman-opencode-plugin/main/setup.sh | bash
Or clone and run locally
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dantesCode/caveman-opencode-plugin/main/setup.sh
bash setup.sh
Or create caveman.json manually:
Project-level config (recommended)
echo '{"enabled":true,"defaultMode":"full","features":{"caveman":true,"commit":true,"review":true}}' > caveman.json
Or global config in ~/.config/opencode/
mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode
echo '{"enabled":true,"defaultMode":"full","features":{"caveman":true,"commit":true,"review":true}}' > ~/.config/opencode/caveman.json
Upstream
Behavior mirrors JuliusBrussee/caveman methodology. See UPSTREAM.md for reference and intentional differences.
Configuration
Or global config in ~/.config/opencode/
caveman.json example:
{
"enabled": true,
"defaultMode": "full",
"features": {
"caveman": true,
"commit": true,
"review": true
}
}
Or global config in ~/.config/opencode/
* enabled — master switch
* defaultMode — mode on session start (lite, full, ultra, wenyan-lite, wenyan-full, wenyan-ultra, off)
* features — toggle individual features:
* caveman — enable caveman communication mode
* commit — enable /caveman-commit command
* review — enable /caveman-review command
Or global config in ~/.config/opencode/
Config file locations
Plugin looks for caveman.json in this order:
1. ./caveman.json (project root)
2. ~/.config/opencode/caveman.json (global)
  Project config takes precedence over global.
Commands
Or global config in ~/.config/opencode/
* Command | Description
* /caveman <mode> | Switch caveman mode
* /caveman-commit <diff> | Generate conventional commit message
* /caveman-review <code> | One-line code review
Modes
Or global config in ~/.config/opencode/
* Mode | Description
* lite | Light compression, keep some filler
* full | Full caveman rules (default)
* ultra | Maximum brevity
* wenyan-lite | Lite in classical Chinese style
* wenyan-full | Full classical Chinese style
* wenyan-ultra | Ultra classical Chinese style
Or global config in ~/.config/opencode/
* off / normal | Disable caveman
Or global config in ~/.config/opencode/
Companion Plugin
For context compression, pair with @tarquinen/opencode-dcp.

MIT

import { tool } from "@opencode-ai/plugin"
import { buildCavemanRules } from "./compress.js"
import { readdir, readFile, mkdir, writeFile, access } from "fs/promises"
import { join, basename, extname } from "path"
import { fileURLToPath } from "url"
import { dirname } from "path"

const __filename = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)
const __dirname = dirname(__filename)
const PKG_ROOT = join(__dirname, "..")

const INJECTED_MARKER = "Respond terse like smart caveman"

async function loadCommandsFromDir(
  dir: string,
): Promise<Record<string, { template: string; description?: string }>> {
  const result: Record<string, { template: string; description?: string }> = {}
  try {
    const files = await readdir(dir)
    for (const file of files) {
      if (extname(file) !== ".md") continue
      const name = basename(file, ".md")
      const content = await readFile(join(dir, file), "utf8")
      result[name] = { template: content.trim() }
    }
  } catch {
    // commands dir missing or unreadable — skip
  }
  return result
}

async function fileExists(p: string): Promise<boolean> {
  try {
    await access(p)
    return true
  } catch {
    return false
  }
}

async function installFilesToConfigDir(): Promise<void> {
  const configDir = process.env.OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR
  if (!configDir) return

  // Install skills/caveman/SKILL.md
  const srcSkill = join(PKG_ROOT, "skills", "caveman", "SKILL.md")
  const destSkillDir = join(configDir, "skills", "caveman")
  const destSkill = join(destSkillDir, "SKILL.md")
  if (!(await fileExists(destSkill))) {
    await mkdir(destSkillDir, { recursive: true })
    const content = await readFile(srcSkill, "utf8")
    await writeFile(destSkill, content, "utf8")
  }

  // Install command/*.md files
  const commandsDir = join(PKG_ROOT, "commands")
  const destCommandDir = join(configDir, "command")
  await mkdir(destCommandDir, { recursive: true })
  const commands = await loadCommandsFromDir(commandsDir)
  for (const [name, cmd] of Object.entries(commands)) {
    const destFile = join(destCommandDir, `${name}.md`)
    if (!(await fileExists(destFile))) {
      await writeFile(destFile, cmd.template, "utf8")
    }
  }
}

const CavemanPlugin = async ({ client, directory }: any) => {
  await installFilesToConfigDir()
  return {
    config: async (config: any) => {
      // Register skills directory
      config.skills = config.skills ?? {}
      config.skills.paths = config.skills.paths ?? []
      const skillsDir = join(PKG_ROOT, "skills")
      if (!config.skills.paths.includes(skillsDir)) {
        config.skills.paths.push(skillsDir)
      }

      // Register commands
      const commands = await loadCommandsFromDir(join(PKG_ROOT, "commands"))
      config.command = config.command ?? {}
      for (const [name, cmd] of Object.entries(commands)) {
        if (!config.command[name]) {
          config.command[name] = cmd
        }
      }
    },

    "experimental.chat.messages.transform": async (_input: any, output: any) => {
      try {
        if (!output.messages?.length) return
        const firstUser = output.messages.find((m: any) => m.info?.role === "user")
        if (!firstUser?.parts?.length) return
        // Only inject once
        if (
          firstUser.parts.some(
            (p: any) => p.type === "text" && p.text?.includes(INJECTED_MARKER),
          )
        )
          return
        const rules = await buildCavemanRules(directory)
        const ref = firstUser.parts[0]
        firstUser.parts.unshift({ ...ref, type: "text", text: rules })
      } catch (err) {
        try {
          await client.app.log({
            body: {
              service: "opencode-caveman",
              level: "error",
              message: String(err),
            },
          })
        } catch {}
      }
    },

    tool: {
      "caveman-compress": tool({
        description:
          "Returns caveman compression rules prepended to your AGENTS.md. Inject the output as session instructions to activate terse mode.",
        args: {},
        async execute(_args: any, _context: any) {
          return buildCavemanRules(directory)
        },
      }),
    },
  }
}

export default {
  id: "opencode-caveman",
  server: CavemanPlugin,
}

import type { Plugin, Hooks } from '@opencode-ai/plugin'
import type { Part } from '@opencode-ai/sdk'
import { loadConfig } from './config'
import { getState, resolveInjection } from './state'
import { getCavemanSystemInstruction } from './skills/caveman'
import { handleCommit } from './commands/commit'
import { handleReview } from './commands/review'
import { handleMode } from './commands/mode'

let configLogged = false

function logConfigOnce(): void {
  if (configLogged) return
  configLogged = true
  const { config, report } = loadConfig()
  console.log(`[caveman] config: project=${report.project} (${report.projectPath}), global=${report.global} (${report.globalPath}), defaultMode=${config.defaultMode}`)
  for (const warning of report.warnings) {
    console.log(`[caveman] warning: ${warning}`)
  }
}

const cavemanPlugin: Plugin = async () => {
  logConfigOnce()

  const hooks: Hooks = {
    config: async (opencodeConfig) => {
      opencodeConfig.command ??= {}
      opencodeConfig.command['caveman'] = { template: '', description: 'Toggle caveman communication mode' }
      opencodeConfig.command['caveman-mode'] = { template: '', description: 'Toggle caveman communication mode' }
      opencodeConfig.command['caveman-commit'] = { template: '', description: 'Generate commit messages in caveman style' }
      opencodeConfig.command['caveman-review'] = { template: '', description: 'Review code in caveman style' }
    },

    'experimental.chat.system.transform': async (input, output) => {
      const { config: cfg } = loadConfig()

      const sessionID = input.sessionID
      if (!sessionID) return

      const decision = resolveInjection(getState(sessionID), cfg.defaultMode)
      if (!cfg.enabled || !cfg.features.caveman) return
      if (!decision.inject) return

      output.system.push(getCavemanSystemInstruction(decision.mode))
    },

    'command.execute.before': async (input, output) => {
      const cmd = (output as any).command ?? input.command
      const args = ((output as any).args ?? input.arguments).trim()
      const sessionID = input.sessionID

      if (cmd === 'caveman' || cmd === 'caveman-mode') {
        const result = handleMode(sessionID, [args])
        output.parts = [{ type: 'text', text: result.message } as Part]
        return
      }

      if (cmd === 'caveman-commit') {
        const result = handleCommit(sessionID, args.split(/\s+/))
        output.parts = [{ type: 'text', text: result.systemInstruction || result.message || '' } as Part]
        return
      }

      if (cmd === 'caveman-review') {
        const result = handleReview(sessionID, args.split(/\s+/))
        output.parts = [{ type: 'text', text: result.systemInstruction || result.message || '' } as Part]
        return
      }
    },
  }

  return hooks
}

export default cavemanPlugin
