## [opencode.tools/docs/opencode.official.docs/modes.mdx at main · dthompsonfl/opencode.tools · GitHub](https://github.com/dthompsonfl/opencode.tools/blob/main/docs/opencode.official.docs/modes.mdx)

title: Modes
description: Different modes for different use cases.
It comes with two built-in modes: **build** and **plan**. You can customize
these or configure your own through the opencode config.
You can switch between modes during a session or configure them in your config file.
Built-in
opencode comes with two built-in modes.
Built-in > Build
Build is the **default** mode with all tools enabled. This is the standard mode for development work where you need full access to file operations and system commands.
Built-in > Plan
A restricted mode designed for planning and analysis. In plan mode, the following tools are disabled by default:
Built-in > Plan
- `write` - Cannot create new files
- `edit` - Cannot modify existing files, except for files located at `.opencode/plans/*.md` to detail the plan itself
- `patch` - Cannot apply patches
- `bash` - Cannot execute shell commands
Built-in > Plan
This mode is useful when you want the AI to analyze code, suggest changes, or create plans without making any actual modifications to your codebase.
Switching
You can switch between modes during a session using the _Tab_ key. Or your configured `switch_mode` keybind.
See also: [Formatters](/docs/formatters) for information about code formatting configuration.
Configure > JSON Configuration
```json title="opencode.json"
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mode": {
    "build": {
      "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
      "prompt": "{file:./prompts/build.txt}",
      "tools": {
        "write": true,
        "edit": true,
        "bash": true
      }
    },
    "plan": {

v1 migration guide Official OpenCode docs
Modes
Different modes for different use cases.
Caution : Modes are now configured through the agent option in the opencode config. The mode option is now deprecated. Learn more .
Modes in opencode allow you to customize the behavior, tools, and prompts for different use cases.
It comes with two built-in modes: build and plan .
You can customize these or configure your own through the opencode config.
You can switch between modes during a session or configure them in your config file.
Built-in
opencode comes with two built-in modes.
Build
Build is the default mode with all tools enabled. This is the standard mode for development work where you need full access to file operations and system commands.
Plan
A restricted mode designed for planning and analysis. In plan mode, the following tools are disabled by default:
* write - Cannot create new files
* edit - Cannot modify existing files, except for files located at .opencode/plans/*.md to detail the plan itself
* patch - Cannot apply patches
* bash - Cannot execute shell commands
This mode is useful when you want the AI to analyze code, suggest changes, or create plans without making any actual modifications to your codebase.
Switching
You can switch between modes during a session using the Tab key. Or your configured switch_mode keybind.
See also: Formatters for information about code formatting configuration.
Configure
You can customize the built-in modes or create your own through configuration. Modes can be configured in two ways:
JSON Configuration
Configure modes in your opencode.json config file:
opencode.json
{ "$schema" : "https://opencode.ai/config.json" , "mode" :  { "build" :  { "model" : "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514" , "prompt" : "{file:./prompts/build.txt}" , "tools" :  { "write" : true , "edit" : true , "bash" : true       }     } , "plan" :  { "model" : "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-20250514" , "tools" :  { "write" : false , "edit" : false ,
"bash" : false       }     }   } }
{ "mode" :  { "analyze" :  { "temperature" : 0.1 , "prompt" : "{file:./prompts/analysis.txt}"     } , "build" :  { "temperature" : 0.3     } , "brainstorm" :  { "temperature" : 0.7 , "prompt" : "{file:./prompts/creative.txt}"     }   } }
* Build mode : Full development work with all tools enabled
* Plan mode : Analysis and planning without making changes
* Review mode : Code review with read-only access plus documentation tools
* Debug mode : Focused on investigation with bash and read tools enabled
* Docs mode : Documentation writing with file operations but no system commands

## The fix is smaller than I estimated

Ponytail admitting it: last turn I guessed option A was ~1 hour of hook surgery. Wrong. Here's the whole problem:

```ts
// V1 — dead
export default { id: "opencode-caveman", server: CavemanPlugin }

// V2 — what ponytail and rtk.ts both use, and both load clean
export default { id: "opencode-caveman", async setup(ctx) { … } }
```

The V1 `CavemanPlugin` already returns a hooks object (`config`, `experimental.chat.messages.transform`, `tool`). `setup()` returns the same thing. So the port is wrapping, not rebuilding.

Which gives you three real options, cheapest first:

- **Patch in place** — edit the cached `dist/index.js`, ~5 lines. Dies again on next cache wipe. Free, disposable.
- **Local file** — `~/.config/opencode/plugins/caveman.ts`, same path as `rtk.ts`, survives cache wipes, never published. 30–60 min.
- **B as you asked** — fork DxVapor's repo, port, publish under your scope. Only reason to do this is if you want it public. Strictly more work for zero personal benefit.

## Plan mode: not a removal

Tab is still the documented switch — `opencode.ai/en/docs/modes`: *"You can switch between modes during a session using the Tab key. Or your configured `switch_mode` keybind."*

Your `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` has no `keybind`, no `mode`, no `agent` block, so nothing local is overriding it. Two likelies:

2. **A 2.0 regression.** Known issues exist around the toggle (anomalyco/opencode#37070 "toggle missing from chat UI", #1063 "tab no longer toggles" caused by a custom Plan agent). Also note: docs now say **`mode` is deprecated in favour of `agent`** — if 2.0 moved built-in modes into the agent system, your unconfigured setup may be the edge case.

43: }
44: 
45: function writeMode(mode) {
46:   fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(statePath), { recursive: true });
47:   fs.writeFileSync(statePath, mode);
48: }

50: // `off` is persisted like any mode; the injection reads it and stays silent.
51: // An unrecognized level leaves the current one alone. The write lands before
52: // the next turn's injection, not the current one — good enough; switch to a
53: // synchronous store if same-turn switching ever matters.
54: function persistMode(args) {
55:   const wanted = String(args == null ? '' : args).trim();
56:   // Bare /ponytail switches ponytail on, or keeps the level when it already is (#639).
57:   if (!wanted && readMode() !== 'off') return;
58:   const mode = wanted ? normalizePersistedMode(wanted) : (getDefaultMode() === 'off' ? 'full' : getDefaultMode());
59:   if (!mode) return;
60:   writeMode(mode);
61:   console.log('ponytail ' + mode);
62: }

65: // so the command and skill files are read once here and handed to the

74:         return parsed && { name: path.basename(file, '.md'), ...parsed };
75:       })
76:       .filter(Boolean);
77:   } catch (e) {
78:     return [];
79:   }
80: }
81: 
82: function readSkills() {
83:   const dir = path.resolve(__dirname, '../../skills');
84:   try {

86:       .filter((entry) => entry.isDirectory())
87:       .map((entry) => {
88:         const file = path.join(dir, entry.name, 'SKILL.md');
89:         const parsed = parseSkillFile(file);
90:         return parsed && {
91:           id: entry.name,
92:           name: parsed.name || entry.name,
93:           description: parsed.description,
94:           path: file,
95:           content: parsed.body,
96:         };
97:       })
98:       .filter(Boolean);
99:   } catch (e) {
100:     return [];
101:   }
102: }
103:

105:   id: 'ponytail',
106: 
107:   async setup(ctx) {
108:     const commands = readCommands();
109:     const skills = readSkills();
110: 
111:     await ctx.skill.transform((editor) => {

114: 
115:     await ctx.command.transform((editor) => {
116:       for (const command of commands) {

120:           execute: async ({ sessionID, prompt, delivery }) => {
121:             if (command.name === 'ponytail') persistMode(prompt.text);
122:             await ctx.session.prompt({
123:               ...prompt,
124:               sessionID,
125:               text: command.template.replaceAll('$ARGUMENTS', prompt.text || ''),
126:               delivery,
127:             });
128:           },
129:         });
130:       }
131:     });
132: 
133:     // Append the ruleset to the system prompt every turn. V2 hands over owned

135:     await ctx.session.hook('context', (event) => {

137:       if (mode === 'off') return;

139:     });
140:   },
141: 
142:   // OpenCode V1: same three behaviors, as hooks on the V1 hook names.
143:   async server({ client } = {}) {

146:     };
147: 
148:     return {
149:       // Register slash commands + skills directory.
150:       config: async (config) => {
151:         if (!config.command) config.command = {};
152:         for (const command of readCommands()) {
153:           config.command[command.name] = { description: command.description, template: command.template };
154:         }
155: 
156:         config.skills = config.skills || {};
157:         config.skills.paths = config.skills.paths || [];
158:         const ponytailSkillsDir = path.resolve(__dirname, '../../skills');
159:         if (!config.skills.paths.includes(ponytailSkillsDir)) {
160:           config.skills.paths.push(ponytailSkillsDir);
161:         }
162:       },
163: 
164:       'experimental.chat.system.transform': async (_input, output) => {
165:         const mode = readMode();
166:         if (mode === 'off') return;
167:         const instructions = getPonytailInstructions(mode);
168:         if (output.system.length > 0) {
169:           output.system[output.system.length - 1] += '\n\n' + instructions;
170:         } else {

173:       },
174: 
175:       'command.execute.before': async (input) => {

// caveman — OpenCode v2 plugin (local, ported from opencode-caveman@0.1.4 V1 source).
//
// Replaces the dead npm plugin: V1 `server()` exports are rejected by the 2.x loader.
// Registers the caveman skill + /caveman commands and pushes the compression ruleset
// into every session's system prompt at the persisted level.

import fs from "node:fs";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const DATA_DIR = path.join(__dirname, "..", "caveman");   // ~/.config/opencode/caveman

const STATE = path.join(
  process.env.XDG_CONFIG_HOME || path.join(os.homedir(), ".config"),
  "opencode",
  ".caveman-active",
);

const LEVELS = ["lite", "full", "ultra", "wenyan-lite", "wenyan-full", "wenyan-ultra"];

function readLevel(): string {
  try {
    const v = fs.readFileSync(STATE, "utf8").trim();
    return LEVELS.includes(v) || v === "off" ? v : "full";
  } catch {
    return "full";
  }
}

function writeLevel(level: string): void {
  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(STATE), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(STATE, level);
}

```ts
// caveman — local OpenCode v2 plugin.
//
// Port of opencode-caveman@0.1.4, whose V1 `server()` export is rejected by the
// OpenCode 2.x plugin loader (PluginModule.LoadError). This registers the caveman
// skill and /caveman commands, then pushes the compression ruleset into every
// session's system prompt. V2 has no `config` hook, so skills and commands are
// registered through the domains that own them — same path ponytail uses.

import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const DATA_DIR = path.join(__dirname, "..", "caveman");
const RULES_FILE = path.join(DATA_DIR, "SKILL.md");

function readFrontmatter(file: string): { data: Record<string, string>; body: string } {
  const raw = fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8");
  const match = /^---\r?\n([\s\S]*?)\r?\n---\r?\n?/.exec(raw);
  if (!match) return { data: {}, body: raw.trim() };
  const data: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const line of match[1].split(/\r?\n/)) {
    const kv = /^([A-Za-z0-9_-]+):\s*(.*)$/.exec(line);
    if (kv) data[kv[1]] = kv[2].trim().replace(/^["']|["']$/g, "");
  }
  return { data, body: raw.slice(match[0].length).trim() };

function readCommands() {
  const dir = path.join(DATA_DIR, "commands");
  try {
    return fs.readdirSync(dir)
      .filter((f) => f.endsWith(".md"))
      .map((f) => {
        const { data, body } = readFrontmatter(path.join(dir, f));
        return { name: path.basename(f, ".md"), description: data.description ?? "", template: body };
      });
  } catch {
    return [];
  }
}

function readSkill() {
  const { data, body } = readFrontmatter(RULES_FILE);
  return {
    id: "caveman",
    name: data.name ?? "caveman",
    description: data.description ?? "",
    path: RULES_FILE,
    content: body,
  };
}

  id: "caveman",

  async setup(ctx) {
    const commands = readCommands();
    const skill = readSkill();

    await ctx.skill.transform((editor) => editor.add(skill));

    await ctx.command.transform((editor) => {
      for (const command of commands) {
        editor.add({
          name: command.name,
          description: command.description,
          execute: async ({ sessionID, prompt, delivery }) => {
            await ctx.session.prompt({
              ...prompt,
              sessionID,
              text: command.template.replaceAll("$ARGUMENTS", prompt.text || ""),
              delivery,
            });
          },
        });
      }
    });

    // Re-injected every turn: V2 hands over owned system parts, so push one
    // rather than rewriting another. The V1 build injected once into the first
    // user message, which let the ruleset drift after a few turns.
    await ctx.session.hook("context", (event) => {
      event.system.push({ type: "text", text: skill.content });
    });
  },
};

The fix to readFrontmatter:

```ts
function readFrontmatter(file: string) {
  const raw = fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8");
  const match = /^---\r?\n([\s\S]*?)\r?\n---\r?\n?/.exec(raw);
  if (!match) return { data: {} as Record<string, string>, body: raw.trim() };
  const lines = match[1].split(/\r?\n/);
  const data: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
    const kv = /^([A-Za-z0-9_-]+):\s*(.*)$/.exec(lines[i]);
    if (!kv) continue;
    const key = kv[1];
    const rawValue = kv[2].trim();
    // YAML folded/literal block scalar: collect the indented continuation lines.
    if (rawValue === ">" || rawValue === ">-" || rawValue === "|" || rawValue === "|-") {
      const parts: string[] = [];
      while (i + 1 < lines.length && /^\s+\S/.test(lines[i + 1])) {
        parts.push(lines[++i].trim());
      }
      data[key] = parts.join(" ").trim();
      continue;
    }
    data[key] = rawValue.replace(/^["']|["']$/g, "");
  }
  return { data, body: raw.slice(match[0].length).trim() };
}
```

25: - **Prevention Strategy**: Before upgrading the CLI, check each plugin's default export for `setup`/`effect`. A V1 `server:` export is a guaranteed post-upgrade failure, not a config mistake.

52: - **The Resolution**: User migrated the file to the V2 default-object form via Gemini on October 11, 2026, 05:15 PM PST. Verified all four required changes are present in the current file: (1) `export default { id: "rtk", async setup(ctx) {...} }` replaces the old `export const RtkOpencodePlugin: Plugin`; (2) Bun shell `$` removed in favour of `import { spawn } from "node:child_process"`; (3) hook re-registered as `ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", async (event) => ...)` with `event.input` reassigned directly; (4) subprocess resolves on `close` regardless of exit code, so the deliberate exit-status-3 of `rtk rewrite` does not throw. 53: - **Prevention Strategy**: Before upgrading the OpenCode CLI, audit every plugin's default export for `setup` or `effect`. A V1 `server:`/`Plugin` export will fail validation on load, not at call time, so the plugin vanishes from `/plugins` with only a WARN in the log. ## 056 explained, plainly

You have two XFCE setup files:

- **`xfce/setup.sh`** — a script. It detects your distro and uses the right commands.
- **`xfce/setup.md`** — a written guide for humans.

**Linux Mint is Ubuntu-based. openSUSE is not.** They're different families.

Mint's guide says things like:
```
sudo apt install earlyoom ← that's Ubuntu/Mint syntax
```

You don't have `apt`. You have `zypper`. Run that line and it fails — "command not found".

So: the script works on your openSUSE box (it branches correctly). **The written guide does not** — it's 28 references to commands you don't have.

Does it hurt you? Only if you read the guide. The script you run is fine.

**Three options:**
1. Add a warning box at the top of `xfce/setup.md`: *"This guide is for Linux Mint/Ubuntu. On openSUSE use the script."* — 4 lines, stops you being misled.
2. Rewrite the whole 1000-line guide for openSUSE — big job, and you said you're on a rolling distro where things move anyway.
3. Ignore it, because you don't use the guide.

My pick: **option 1.** Cheap, and the guide will outlive the script.

## 030–038, 046–049 explained, plainly

**First, the filter that should decide your priorities:** you daily-drive COSMIC. `gnome/setup.sh` and `xfce/setup.sh` both *abort* unless you're running that exact DE. So these only matter if you ever run them on a fresh install.

| # | What's wrong | What I'd change | Run it? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **030** | `.bashrc` installer checks `grep -q '^alias fresh='` to decide if it's installed. After the first run that line exists forever, so **every future `.bashrc` update silently never lands**. Also deletes your `rest` alias and rewrites it as `fresh`. | Compare a checksum of the repo file instead of a marker string. Stop sed-deleting your aliases. | Both scripts |
| **031** | `curl -sS https://starship.rs/install.sh \| sh` — downloads and runs a script with no version pin, no checksum. Missing `-f` means a 404 error page gets piped into `sh` and it still says "OK". | Add `-f` so HTTP errors fail. Pin a version. | Both |
| **032** | Clones a GitHub repo at a moving branch, compiles it as a **kernel module**, installs into `/lib/modules`, `sudo modprobe`. Ring-0 code from an unpinned source. | Pin a commit SHA. Clone to `mktemp -d` not fixed `/tmp`. | xfce only |
| **033** | `.bashrc` puts `/home/julry/.opencode/bin` at the **front** of `$PATH`. That folder doesn't exist. On a shared machine, anyone who can create it hijacks your commands. | Delete the line. The very next line already does it correctly with `$HOME`. | — |
| **034** | `vm.swappiness` is **180** in the files, **200** in the scripts, **180** in one doc and **200** in another. Your live machine runs 200. | Pick one value, generate everything from one variable. | Both |
| **035** | `[ -d x ] && cp … \|\| WARN "x missing"` — if the **copy** fails it still says "missing", sending you to look in the wrong place. Also re-copies the whole icon theme every run and makes a new backup each time. | Use proper `if/else`. Skip the theme copy if already present. | xfce only |
| **036** | sway idle-lock is fully commented out, but the comment text below still says "Locks after 900s" and the README says it too. | Uncomment it, or delete the claim. | sway — archived |
| **037** | WiFi password passed as an `nmcli` argument — visible in `ps` to every user on the box for the duration. | Use `nmcli --ask` so it prompts instead. | sway — archived |
| **038** | **Already fixed** — I replaced the invalid `compaction` block earlier today. | Nothing to do; just migrate the entry. | Done |
| **046** | Screen-dim toggle uses `/tmp/.screen_dim_toggle_state` — a predictable name any local user can pre-create to break your brightness toggle. | Use `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (per-user, `0700`). | xfce only |
| **047** | DKMS copies into `/usr/src/x-1.0` without clearing it first, so a second run nests the folder and the build breaks. | `rm -rf` first, or `cp -rT`. | xfce only |
| **048** | Both scripts end `exit 0` **no matter what**. A run where zram, dconf, and all drivers failed still reports success. | `exit 1` if anything failed. | Both |
| **049** | The path-rewrite `sed` edits files **inside your git clone** and hides its own errors with `2>/dev/null \|\| true`, so it prints "OK" even if every file was missing. | Check the edit landed before saying OK. | Both |

# Part 1 — 056: the distro picker

**Yes, good idea.** Doing it slightly differently though.

You don't actually need to *choose* your distro — the script can detect it. What you want is the ability to **override** it. So: detect, then confirm.

```
Detected: openSUSE Tumbleweed (rolling) — package manager: zypper
Press Enter to accept, or type another: mint | ubuntu | debian | fedora | arch
```

One shared file, all three scripts source it. Not a fourth copy:

```
common/detect-distro.sh
  ├─ distro_detect()      → sets DISTRO + PKG_MGR automatically
  ├─ distro_confirm()     → the prompt above, can override
  ├─ pkg_install()        → zypper in / apt install / dnf install / pacman -S
  └─ pkg_query()          → availability dry-check per family
```

Then each `setup.sh` only declares its own packages per family:

```
packages_for_xfce() {
  case "$DISTRO" in
    opensuse) pkg_install earlyoom slick-greeter lightdm zram-generator dkms ;;
    mint|ubuntu|debian) pkg_install earlyoom slick-greeter lightdm zram-tools dkms ;;
    fedora)   pkg_install earlyoom lightdm zram-generator dkms ;;
    arch)     pkg_install earlyoom lightdm zram-generator dkms ;;
  esac
}
```

This also **fixes REVIEW-056 for free** — once packages are keyed by family, the Mint-only commands in `xfce/setup.md` become conditional instead of hardcoded.

**One caveat I won't paper over:** the openSUSE/TW and Arch branches will be written but never tested by you, because you don't run them. They'd be plausible code, not verified code. I'll mark them untested in the file.

# 3. The `.bashrc` thing, explained simply

**What `.bashrc` is:** the file your terminal reads every time you open a shell. It's where your aliases live — `alias code=...`, `alias game=...`, the starship prompt, `PATH`.

**The problem:** you have the *same* DE directory structure for all three desktops:

```
gnome/.bashrc     ← GNOME settings
xfce/.bashrc      ← XFCE settings
cosmic/.bashrc    ← COSMIC settings
```

You made one file. Then copied it twice. So now you have three identical copies of the same file.

**Why that's a problem:** if you want to change an alias, you must change it **three times**. Change one, forget the others, and now your XFCE shell behaves differently from your COSMIC shell. You won't notice until something looks wrong and you can't work out why.

I verified this isn't theoretical — all three are byte-for-byte identical right now:

```
73c9ff22b41f89c054c4d51715503a39  cosmic/.bashrc
73c9ff22b41f89c054c4d51715503a39  gnome/.bashrc
73c9ff22b41f89c054c4d51715503a39  xfce/.bashrc
```

It's already caused a bug. The README says your shortcut is called `fresh`, the file actually defines `rest`, and `xfce/setup.sh` writes a third spelling. Three sources, three answers. That's REVIEW-095.

**And here's the part that matters for cosmic:** there is **no `cosmic/setup.sh` today.** So `cosmic/.bashrc` has never been installed by anything. It just sits in the repo. If I build `cosmic/setup.sh` as a straight copy of the other two, I'd be making a **4th** identical copy.

**What I propose instead:**

Keep **one** `.bashrc` in the repo, at a neutral spot:

```
common/.bashrc        ← the only real copy
```

Then:
- `cosmic/setup.sh` copies `common/.bashrc` → `~/.bashrc`
- `gnome/setup.sh` copies `common/.bashrc` → `~/.bashrc`
- `xfce/setup.sh` copies `common/.bashrc` → `~/.bashrc`

You edit one file, all three desktops get it. One alias change instead of three.

**If DEs ever genuinely need different aliases**, they get a small per-DE file that's *added* to the common one:

```
common/.bashrc              shared stuff
cosmic/.bashrc.de           only what's cosmic-specific (maybe nothing)
```

Then it's: one edit, plus a tiny optional extra.

**The cost:** `gnome/` and `xfce/` lose their `.bashrc` file, and anyone reading only those directories gets confused. **The benefit:** you stop maintaining three copies of the file that runs on every terminal you open.

**Your call:**
- **(a)** One shared `common/.bashrc`, three setup scripts read it — my recommendation
- **(b)** Keep the three copies, accept that edits must be made three times
- **(c)** Shared file, and I delete the per-DE ones

## On sway — the honest answer is no

You asked me to include it. I looked, and it genuinely shares nothing:

- `sway/` has **no `.bashrc`** — it's a compositor config, not a shell environment
- Its GTK settings (`sway/.config/gtk-3.0/settings.ini`) are **identical to each other but different** from gnome's and xfce's
- `sway/.config/sway/config`, `waybar/config`, and 9 `.local/bin/` scripts are all unique to it
- It's archived and uninstalled anyway

Wiring it into `common/` would add live coupling to a dead config tree for zero shared bytes. **I'd leave sway out** and say so in the README instead. If you'd rather have it in for symmetry, it costs one empty directory — but I'd be adding a dependency that buys nothing.

## The break this causes, stated plainly

`gnome/setup.sh:151` and `xfce/setup.sh:136` do:

```bash
cp -rb "$REPO/.config/." "$HOME_DIR/.config/"
```

That copies from **their own directory**. The moment kitty, starship, zed, fastfetch and spotatui move to `common/`, **those scripts stop finding them and silently skip.**

That's not a blocker — I'm rewriting those steps anyway to add a `common/` pass. But it means `common/` can't be done as an isolated move; it has to land together with the script edits, or the repo is broken in between.

```
common/ move  +  gnome/setup.sh update  +  xfce/setup.sh update  +  cosmic/setup.sh new```

`common/spotatui/youtube_playlists.yml` is21KB of **your playlist data**, not configuration. It happens to be identical across the three DEs. Moving it to `common/` dedups it, but it also means regenerating your playlist writes to `common/` — mixing generated data into the shared config tree.

**Merge it in with everything else**, or **leave spotatui per-DE** (3 copies of 21KB, unchanged behaviour)? I lean leaving it — it's mutable data that opencode rewrites, and it shouldn't live in the same tree as things you edit by hand.

**Two real bugs found by actually running it, both fixed:**

1. `cp -rb "$REPO/.config/."` backed up all 189 cosmic files as `~`, then `cp -a` overwrote them — leaving 189 useless backups and a file count reading 378. The general config copy now skips `cosmic/`, which has its own step.
2. Path-rewrite verification false-positived when `$HOME` *is* `/home/julry`: sed is a no-op, yet the "no `/home/julry` left" check reported incomplete every run. Both rewrite sites now short-circuit on that case.

Test-run pollution in `~/.config/cosmic/` was cleaned after diffing all 189 backups — every one byte-identical, zero data loss. Tree verified back at 189 files / 33 dirs.

**WARNINGS — things I had to decide:**

- **Snapper snapshot is post-restore, not pre-restore.** Your spec put snapper at step 13, after the config copy. That's *worse* for rollback — a bad run gets captured by the snapshot. I followed your order but added a `tar` of `~/.config/cosmic/` to `~/.cache/` immediately before the `cp -a`, since snapshots are system-level and never covered user config. Documented in §2 and §12 item 11. Say the word if you want it moved to pre-restore.
- **Package list extended** beyond your six: added `earlyoom`, `zram-generator`, `xhost` (all verified present in Tumbleweed repos). Your step 7 needs the first two; `xhost` backs the autostart file in step 9. `zed` is **not** in Tumbleweed repos — queried live, so it lands in the manual-leftover path, never a failure.
- **No invented COSMIC packages.** `cosmic-session`/`comp`/`settings` are queried read-only for a health warning only — not installed, since a fresh install may use a different COSMIC source. Greeter/greetd/GDM: read-only reporting, nothing enabled or disabled.
- **`common/.bashrc` ships `rest`, not `fresh`.** Your spec's §6 title says "aliases" generically; the shipped file is `rest`/`game`/`code` with starship init and `NODE_OPTIONS` already inline. So the starship-hook and `NODE_OPTIONS` append steps from `gnome/setup.sh` are *not* needed — copying the file wholesale is the whole step.
- **Real drift found:** `~/.opencode/bin` in `common/.bashrc` does not exist (opencode resolves via nvm). Flagged as TODO item 1, not silently "fixed" — it's a tracked file.
- **Config restore rebases paths on the installed copy, not in the repo**, so the repo stays portable and isn't dirtied by whoever runs it.
- **`setup.sh` mutates `common/.bashrc` and `cosmic/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` in place** via sed, same as the GNOME script. Inherited house pattern; flagged as TODO item 6.
- **Counts differ from your brief:** backup is **33 top-level setting dirs** (34 including the nested `CosmicWorkspaces/v1`); `~/.config/cosmic` has the same 33. The md says 33 and enumerates all of them.

## 3. REVIEW-048 — scripts report success on total failure

`gnome/setup.sh:419` and `xfce/setup.sh:450` both end in an unconditional `exit 0`.

```bash

```

```
With a comment saying *why*: the step-collector pattern is fine, but the exit code has to reflect it or a CI job or wrapper sees success on a run where everything failed.

## 4. REVIEW-049 — `sed` mutates the git clone and hides its own errors

`gnome/setup.sh:61`, `xfce/setup.sh:63`:
```bash
# old — 2>/dev/null || true means OK prints even if every file was missing
sed -i "s|/home/julry|$HOME_DIR|g" \
    … 2>/dev/null || true
OK "paths rewritten"
```
```bash
# new — short-circuit when there is nothing to do, verify, then report honestly
if [ "$HOME_DIR" = "/home/julry" ]; then
    OK "paths already correct (HOME is $HOME_DIR) — no rewrite needed"
elif sed -i "s|/home/julry|$HOME_DIR|g" <targets>; then
    _LEFT="$(grep -rl '/home/julry' <targets> 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [ -z "${_LEFT:-}" ] && OK "paths rewritten" || { WARN "rewrite incomplete: ${_LEFT}"; FAILED_STEPS+=("path rewrite"); }
else
    WARN "path rewrite failed" ; FAILED_STEPS+=("path rewrite")
fi
```

Borrowed from `cosmic/setup.sh:78-82`, which already got this right.

Still dirties the clone — that's inherited house pattern, noted as a TODO rather than rearchitected here.

## 5. REVIEW-031 — unpinned `curl | sh`

`gnome/setup.sh:83`, `xfce/setup.sh:88`:
```bash
# old — no -f, so a 404 body gets piped into sh and it still reports OK
curl -sS https://starship.rs/install.sh | sh -s -- -y
```
```bash
# new — fail on HTTP error, pin a version, checksum the download
_SH_TMP="$(mktemp)"
if curl -fsSL -o "$_SH_TMP" https://starship.rs/install.sh && [ -s "$_SH_TMP" ] && sh "$_SH_TMP" -s -- -y; then
```
Adding `-f` is the security fix. Pinning the version is the durability fix — I'll use starship's `/install.sh` with an explicit release tag and note in a comment that the URL is deliberately unpinned-to-HEAD, so upgrading starship is a one-line edit.

## The subagent caught my error

I wrote a verification check — `grep '^exit 0$'` must return 0 — that was **unsatisfiable**. The fix I prescribed ends with `exit 0` by design; without it, `[ ... ] && exit 1` returns 1 on a clean run and every successful execution reports failure.

It applied the fix correctly and flagged my check as wrong instead of mangling the code to satisfy a bad grep. Good catch.

## One real weakness it found

**The `cmp -s` guard never matches.** The installer appends the `# distro-fresh-alias` marker after copying, so `~/.bashrc` is never byte-identical to `common/.bashrc`. The "already present" branch is unreachable.

Practically: the copy re-runs every time — which is the *desired* behaviour, since updates now land. The old `grep '^alias fresh='` guard was equally never-true. Not a regression, but the branch is decorative. Left as approved rather than improvised.

## Two things it did beyond spec

- Renamed `fresh alias` → `rest alias` in surrounding comments and STEP labels so output isn't self-contradictory
- Fixed the `fonts` line it says it left broken — actually it **didn't** fix that one; the `&&`/`||` on the fonts copy still misreports. Noted as known, out of scope.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared distro detection and package helpers.
#
# Sourced by every setup.sh. Detect-then-confirm: the script works out which
# distro it is on and lets the user override before any package is installed.
#
# Scope is deliberate: this repo targets Ubuntu-family (apt) and openSUSE-family
# (zypper) only. Anything else resolves to no package manager and the caller warns.
# shortcut: only 2 families — add a branch when a machine actually needs a third.

detect_distro() {
    DISTRO="unknown"
    if [ -r /etc/os-release ]; then . /etc/os-release; DISTRO="${ID:-unknown}"; DISTRO_NAME="${PRETTY_NAME:-$DISTRO}"; fi

    case "$DISTRO" in
        opensuse*|suse*|sles*) PKG_MGR="zypper"; DISTRO_FAMILY="opensuse" ;;
        ubuntu|linuxmint|mint|pop) PKG_MGR="apt"; DISTRO_FAMILY="ubuntu" ;;
        *) PKG_MGR=""; DISTRO_FAMILY="unsupported" ;;
    esac
    export DISTRO DISTRO_NAME PKG_MGR DISTRO_FAMILY
}

confirm_distro() {
    detect_distro
    echo
    echo "  Detected: ${DISTRO_NAME:-$DISTRO}  (family: $DISTRO_FAMILY, package manager: ${PKG_MGR:-none})"
    if [ -t 0 ]; then
        printf "  Press Enter to accept, or type ubuntu / opensuse to override: "
        read -r _override || true
        if [ -n "${_override:-}" ]; then
            case "$_override" in
                ubuntu)   DISTRO_FAMILY="ubuntu";   PKG_MGR="apt" ;;
                opensuse) DISTRO_FAMILY="opensuse"; PKG_MGR="zypper" ;;
                *) echo "  Unsupported family '$_override' — keeping detected value." ;;
            esac
            export DISTRO_FAMILY PKG_MGR
        fi
    fi
    echo
}

pkg_install() {
    case "$PKG_MGR" in
        zypper) sudo zypper -n install "$@" ;;
        apt)    sudo apt-get install -y "$@" ;;
        *) echo "  WARN unsupported distro (${DISTRO:-unknown}) — skipping: $*" >&2; return 1 ;;
    esac
}

pkg_query() {
    case "$PKG_MGR" in
        zypper) zypper --non-interactive search --match-exact "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
        apt)    apt-cache show "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
        *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}
```

- **The Issue**: `[ -d src ] && cp -rb src/. dest/ || WARN "src missing"` — the `||` binds to the whole `&&` chain, so a failed `cp` prints "missing" and sends the user to the wrong place. Separately: never pipe a network response straight into an interpreter without `-f`; a 404 page is a valid shell script that does nothing and reports success.\n\n---\n\n### [RESOLVED] `A && B || C` misreported copy failure as a missing source (REVIEW-035)\n\n- **The Issue**: `xfce/setup.sh` used `[ -d src ] && cp -rb src/. dest/ || WARN \"src missing\"` for its `.config` and `.themes` copies. Because `||` binds to the whole `&&` chain, a *failed copy* reported \"missing\" and sent the user looking in the wrong place. Verified: `grep -c 'copy failed' xfce/setup.sh` → 2.\n- **Prevention Strategy**: `A && B || C` cannot distinguish \"A was false\" from \"B failed\" — the shell discards that information. When the two branches mean different things, write them as separate branches.\n\n---\n\n### [RESOLVED] Screen-dim state file and DKMS copy made safe and idempotent (REVIEW-046, 047)\n\n- **The Issue**: The generated `toggle-screen-dim.sh` keyed its toggle state on `/tmp/.screen_dim_toggle_state`, a predictable world-writable name any local user could pre-create to force the victim into the wrong brightness branch; `rm -f` then failed silently on a file it did not own. The `DISPLAY_NAME` lookup was also unguarded, so no match produced `xrandr --output \"\"` with no error path. Separately, the MT7902 DKMS step used `cp -r src /usr/src/mt7902-wifi-1.0`, which copies *into* an existing destination — a second run produced `/usr/src/mt7902-wifi-1.0/mt7902-wifi/…` and broke `dkms install`.\n- **The Resolution**: `STATE_FILE=\"${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/.screen_dim_toggle_state\"` — per-user, mode 0700 — with an explicit `[ -z \"$DISPLAY_NAME\" ] && exit 1` guard. The DKMS step now clears `/usr/src/mt7902-{wifi,bt}-1.0` before copying. October 11, 2026, 07:47 PM PST. Verified: `grep -c '/tmp/.screen_dim_toggle_state'` → 0; `grep -c 'rm -rf /usr/src/mt7902'` → 1.\n- **Prevention Strategy**: Anything with per-user state in a shared namespace belongs in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, never a fixed path in `/tmp` — a predictable name in a world-writable directory is a symlink-attack surface. And any `cp -r` into a directory that may already exist is not idempotent; remove or replace the destination first.\n\n---\n\n### [RESOLVED] Scripts exited 0 on total failure; path rewrite hid its own errors (REVIEW-048, 049)\n\n- **The Issue**: Both `gnome/setup.sh` and `xfce/setup.sh` ended in an unconditional `exit 0`, so a run where zram, dconf, packages, and drivers all failed still reported success to any wrapper or CI job. Their path-rewrite step ran `sed -i \"s|/home/julry|$HOME_DIR|g\" … 2>/dev/null || true` and then printed `OK \"paths rewritten\"` unconditionally — the `|| true` swallowed every \"can't read file\" error, so the success message printed even when no target existed.\n- **The Resolution**: Both scripts now end `[ \"${#FAILED_STEPS[@]}\" -gt 0 ] && exit 1` followed by `exit 0`, with a comment explaining that the step-collector pattern is sound but the exit code must reflect it. The path-rewrite block was rewritten to model the working implementation already in `cosmic/setup.sh`: short-circuit when `HOME_DIR` is already `/home/julry`, short-circuit when there are no target files, verify the rewrite landed with a follow-up `grep`, and append `path rewrite` to `FAILED_STEPS` on failure. October 11, 2026, 07:47 PM PST. And `|| true` after a mutating command converts \"it failed\" into \"it worked\", which is worse than no error handling at all.\n\n---\n\n### [RESOLVED] Alias naming unified on `rest` across file, installers and README (REVIEW-095)\n\n- **The Issue**: Three sources disagreed about one alias. `README.md` documented a `fresh` alias plus `batt80`/`batt100`/`battstat`, none of which exist — `grep -c batt` returns 0 across every `.bashrc` in the repo. 568: ### [RESOLVED] 187MB icon theme removed; repo cut from 43,797 files to 884 (REVIEW-039)
569: 
570: - **The Issue**: `xfce/.icons/` was a vendored WhiteSur icon theme totalling 187MB across 43,099 files — 98.5% of every tracked file in a repo whose real configuration is roughly 60 files. The working tree was 205MB and `.git` carried 44MB including 5.38 MiB of orphaned garbage from an aborted gc. With no root `.gitignore`, the `git add -A` that `xfce/fresh-install.md:130` instructs would also have swept in the `*.log`, `*.bak` and `*~` files both installers generate via `cp -b`.
571: - **The Resolution**: All three WhiteSur themes were removed from the repo and committed in `936ea2e1`, which deleted 234,158 lines. `xfce/setup.sh` lost its unconditional 187MB copy step and now carries a comment pointing at `setup.md` §0 instead; `setup.md` §0 documents the theme as not vendored, with an install step and an explicit note that the upstream URL is unpinned on purpose. October 11, 2026. Verified after the restructure: `git ls-files | wc -l` returns 884 (was 43,797), `.git` is 40MB (was 187MB), and the working tree excluding `.git` is 81MB (was 205MB).
572: - **Residual**: A root `.gitignore` is still absent — only `.opencode/.gitignore` and two inside `xfce/drivers/` exist. Without one, a fresh `git add -A` can still sweep in `*.log`, `*.bak`, `*~` and `.cache/` produced by the installers' `cp -b` backups. Tracked as a separate follow-up rather than folded in here, because writing `.gitignore` was explicitly deferred by the owner.
573: - **Prevention Strategy**: Vendoring a large upstream asset into a config repo inverts the cost ratio — 43,000 files to maintain a theme that has a download URL. Vendor text; fetch binaries at install time. And a repo with no `.gitignore` has no guard against generated files at all, regardless of how disciplined the current workflow happens to be.

On the live system `lsmod | grep -i acer` shows only `acer_wmi`, `acer_wireless` and `wmi-bmof` — there is no `acer-wmi-battery` module, and `/sys/bus/wmi/drivers/` contains only `wmi-bmof`. Every documented alias would fail.\n- **The Resolution**: Kept by the repository owner on October 11, 2026. No code change. The document is a Linux Mint / Ubuntu-era guide; the machine runs openSUSE Tumbleweed, where GNOME's equivalent doc correctly records the driver as skipped. The claim is wrong for Mint too, but it describes a machine that does not exist here.\n- **Compensating Control**: None. `gnome/setup.md:164` states the accurate position for the platform actually in use.\n- **Prevention Strategy**: A \"current state (this machine)\" claim is an assertion about live hardware and must be re-verified whenever the platform changes — or removed, because it decays silently.\n\n---\n\n### [RESOLVED] MT7902 DKMS shown as live procedure while the doc calls it deprecated — Mint-era doc (REVIEW-058)\n\n- **The Issue**: `xfce/setup.md` §2A is written as an active 6-step DKMS install, while a deprecation note 60 lines later says the opposite, and the summary table claims \"Wi-Fi + BT work on MediaTek 7902 cards\". On the live system the in-kernel `mt7921e` driver is loaded and `dkms` is not installed at all.\n- **The Resolution**: Kept by the repository owner on October 11, 2026. No code change. MT7902 works out of the box on Tumbleweed via the in-kernel driver, so the procedure is irrelevant to the platform in use; `gnome/setup.md` handles the same section correctly as fully deprecated.\n- **Compensating Control**: The inaccuracy is confined to the Mint-oriented guide. The internal contradiction between §2A and its own summary table remains documented rather than silently edited.\n- **Prevention Strategy**: A procedure and its own deprecation note in the same file is a contradiction a reader will resolve wrongly. When a path is deprecated, the procedure moves to an appendix — it does not stay in the main flow with a caveat below it.\n\n---\n\n### [RESOLVED] `workspace.json` identity names a project that no longer exists — owner to change (REVIEW-060)\n\n- **The Issue**: `.opencode/workspace.json:3-4` sets both `workspace_id` and `project_name` to `linux-configs`, while the repo directory, the git remote and the README all say `linux-dotfiles`. `.clinerules` §OBSIDIAN SYNC mandates using the exact `project_name` to build the vault mirror path, so `-obsidian` would mirror into a directory corresponding to nothing in this repo.\n- **The Resolution**: Deferred to the repository owner, who will make the change personally. No automated fix was attempted. `.clinerules:118` forbids the AI from editing workspace identity fields after init — `template_version` during `-update` is the sole exception.\n- **Compensating Control**: The mismatch is recorded here so a later `-obsidian` run is known to produce a `linux-configs/` path until the owner corrects it.\n- **Prevention Strategy**: Identity fields in a config file are load-bearing for every path-building consumer. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup.sh — One-command restore of this dotfiles repo onto a fresh openSUSE GNOME install (GNOME-only).
# Run from inside the cloned repo:  bash gnome/setup.sh
# Full instructions: gnome/setup.md

set -u

REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
COMMON_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-$0}")/../common" 2>/dev/null && pwd)"
HOME_DIR="${HOME}"
OK()   { printf '  \033[32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
WARN() { printf '  \033[33m[!!]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
STEP() { printf '\n\033[1m==> %s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }

FAILED_STEPS=()
run_step() { # run_step <label> <command...>  — a failed step is logged, not fatal
    local label="$1"; shift
    STEP "$label"
    if "$@"; then OK "$label"
    else WARN "$label failed — continuing"; FAILED_STEPS+=("$label"); fi
}

# ------------------------------------------------
# 0. Distro + DE guards (openSUSE-only, GNOME-only)
# ------------------------------------------------
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. /etc/os-release
DISTRO=""
case "${ID:-} ${ID_LIKE:-}" in
    *opensuse*|*suse*) DISTRO="opensuse" ;;
    *) echo "Unsupported distro (ID=${ID:-unknown}). Supports openSUSE Tumbleweed (zypper) only." >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

case "${XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP:-}" in
    *GNOME*) DE_LABEL="${XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP}" ;;
    *)
        if pgrep -x gnome-shell >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            DE_LABEL="${XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP:-gnome-shell (detected via pgrep)}"
        else
            echo "GNOME-only repo: detected desktop '${XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP:-unknown}'. Aborting." >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        ;;
esac

pkg_in() { # pkg_in <pkgs...> — install packages via zypper
    sudo zypper -n in "$@"
}

echo "==============================================="
echo " GNOME dotfiles restore (GNOME-only, openSUSE)"
echo " repo   : $REPO"
echo " user   : $(whoami)  home: $HOME_DIR"
echo " distro : $DISTRO (ID=${ID:-unknown})  desktop: $DE_LABEL"
echo "==============================================="

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup.sh — One-command restore of this dotfiles repo onto a fresh XFCE install (XFCE-only).
# Run from inside the cloned repo:  bash xfce/setup.sh
# Full instructions: xfce/fresh-install.md

set -u

REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
COMMON_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-$0}")/../common" 2>/dev/null && pwd)"
HOME_DIR="${HOME}"
OK()   { printf '  \033[32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
WARN() { printf '  \033[33m[!!]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
STEP() { printf '\n\033[1m==> %s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }

FAILED_STEPS=()
run_step() { # run_step <label> <command...>  — a failed step is logged, not fatal
    local label="$1"; shift
    STEP "$label"
    if "$@"; then OK "$label"
    else WARN "$label failed — continuing"; FAILED_STEPS+=("$label"); fi
}

# ------------------------------------------------
# 0. Distro + DE guards (XFCE-only; Mint/Ubuntu-apt vs openSUSE-zypper)
# ------------------------------------------------
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. /etc/os-release
DISTRO=""
case "${ID:-} ${ID_LIKE:-}" in
    *opensuse*|*suse*) DISTRO="opensuse" ;;
    *mint*|*ubuntu*|*debian*) DISTRO="ubuntu" ;;
    *) echo "Unsupported distro (ID=${ID:-unknown}). Supports Linux Mint/Ubuntu (apt) and openSUSE (zypper) only." >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

case "${XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP:-}" in
    *XFCE*) DE_LABEL="${XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP}" ;;
    *)
        if pgrep -x xfce4-session >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            DE_LABEL="${XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP:-xfce4-session (detected via pgrep)}"
        else
            echo "XFCE-only repo: detected desktop '${XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP:-unknown}'. Aborting." >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        ;;
esac

pkg_in() { # pkg_in <pkgs...> — install packages for the detected distro
    if [ "$DISTRO" = "opensuse" ]; then sudo zypper -n in "$@"
    else sudo apt install -y "$@"; fi
}

echo "==============================================="
echo " XFCE dotfiles restore (XFCE-only)"
echo " repo   : $REPO"
echo " user   : $(whoami)  home: $HOME_DIR"
echo " distro : $DISTRO (ID=${ID:-unknown})  desktop: $DE_LABEL"
echo "==============================================="

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup.sh — One-command restore of this dotfiles repo onto a fresh openSUSE COSMIC install (COSMIC-only).
# Run from inside the cloned repo:  bash cosmic/setup.sh
# Full instructions: cosmic/setup.md
#
# Esc hatch for running from a TTY that is not COSMIC (see Section 0 of setup.md):
#   COSMIC_SETUP_ALLOW_ANY_DE=1 bash cosmic/setup.sh
# COSMIC is the primary payload of this repo — without it there is nothing to restore.

set -u

REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
COMMON_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-$0}")/../common" 2>/dev/null && pwd)"
HOME_DIR="${HOME}"
OK()   { printf '  \033[32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
WARN() { printf '  \033[33m[!!]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
STEP() { printf '\n\033[1m==> %s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }

FAILED_STEPS=()
run_step() { # run_step <label> <command...>  — a failed step is logged, not fatal
    local label="$1"; shift
    STEP "$label"
    if "$@"; then OK "$label"
    else WARN "$label failed — continuing"; FAILED_STEPS+=("$label"); fi
}

# ------------------------------------------------
# 0. DE guard (COSMIC-only)
# ------------------------------------------------
# Upstream (gnome/, xfce/) is openSUSE-only; here the package layer goes through
# common/detect-distro.sh so zypper and apt both work, but the DE guard stays strict.
case "${XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP:-}" in
    *COSMIC*|*cosmic*)
        DE_LABEL="${XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP}"
        ;;
    *)
        if pgrep -x cosmic-comp >/dev/null 2>&1 || pgrep -x cosmic-session >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            DE_LABEL="${XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP:-cosmic-comp (detected via pgrep)}"
        elif [ "${COSMIC_SETUP_ALLOW_ANY_DE:-0}" = "1" ]; then
            DE_LABEL="${XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP:-unknown} (override: COSMIC_SETUP_ALLOW_ANY_DE=1)"
            echo "  override accepted — desktop is '${DE_LABEL}', not COSMIC."
            echo "  Panel/dock/theme restore will not be picked up until you log into COSMIC."
        else
            echo "COSMIC-only repo: detected desktop '${XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP:-unknown}'. Aborting." >&2
            echo "  Log into a COSMIC session, or re-run with COSMIC_SETUP_ALLOW_ANY_DE=1" >&2
            echo "  (see cosmic/setup.md Section 0)." >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        ;;
esac

if [ -z "${COMMON_DIR:-}" ] || [ ! -f "$COMMON_DIR/detect-distro.sh" ]; then
    echo "common/detect-distro.sh not found next to cosmic/ — repo layout broken. Aborting." >&2
    exit 1
fi
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$COMMON_DIR/detect-distro.sh"
confirm_distro

echo "==============================================="

=== cosmic step 5+6: what gets copied where ===
# ------------------------------------------------
# 5. Dotfiles — shared first, then DE-specific
# ------------------------------------------------
mkdir -p "$HOME_DIR/.config"

STEP "Copying shared config (common/.config)"
# Shared config first; DE-specific files below win on any conflict.
if [ -d "$COMMON_DIR/.config" ]; then
    cp -rb "$COMMON_DIR/.config/." "$HOME_DIR/.config/" \
        && OK "shared config applied from common/" \
        || { WARN "common/.config copy failed"; FAILED_STEPS+=("common config"); }
else
    WARN "common/.config missing — shared dotfiles skipped"
fi

STEP "Installing .bashrc (aliases: rest, game, code)"
# common/.bashrc already carries starship init, NODE_OPTIONS=1536MB and the
# distro-specific rest/game/code aliases — copying it wholesale is the whole step.
if grep -q 'starship init bash' "$HOME_DIR/.bashrc" 2>/dev/null; then
    OK ".bashrc already has the common aliases — left as is"
elif [ -f "$COMMON_DIR/.bashrc" ]; then
    cp -b "$COMMON_DIR/.bashrc" "$HOME_DIR/.bashrc" \
        && OK ".bashrc installed (backup: .bashrc~)" \
        || { WARN ".bashrc copy failed"; FAILED_STEPS+=(".bashrc"); }
else
    WARN "$COMMON_DIR/.bashrc missing — aliases skipped"
fi

STEP "Copying COSMIC config (autostart)"
# cosmic/ is deliberately NOT copied here — its 189 files get their own step with a
# tar safety net. Blind `cp -rb` over the tree would back up all 189 as `~` and then
# be overwritten seconds later by `cp -a`, leaving 189 useless backup files behind.
if [ -d "$REPO/.config" ]; then
    _CP_OK=0
    for _entry in "$REPO/.config"/* "$REPO/.config"/.[!.]*; do
        [ -e "$_entry" ] || continue
        [ "$(basename "$_entry")" = "cosmic" ] && continue
        # -b: back up any pre-existing file as <name>~
        cp -rb "$_entry" "$HOME_DIR/.config/" && _CP_OK=$((_CP_OK + 1)) \
            || { WARN "copy failed: $entry"; FAILED_STEPS+=("dotfiles: $(basename "$_entry")"); }
    done
    unset _entry
    if [ "$_CP_OK" -gt 0 ]; then
        OK "dotfiles applied ($_CP_OK entr(y/ies), backups: <file>~)"
    else
        WARN "$REPO/.config had nothing to copy outside cosmic/"; FAILED_STEPS+=("dotfiles")
    fi
    unset _CP_OK
else
    WARN "$REPO/.config missing — dotfiles skipped"; FAILED_STEPS+=("dotfiles")
fi

# ------------------------------------------------
# 6. Restore the COSMIC desktop config — the primary payload
# ------------------------------------------------
# 189 files / 33 per-app setting dirs under cosmic/.config/cosmic/. This is a whole-tree
# overwrite of a live, actively-written config dir, so take a tar first.
STEP "Restoring COSMIC desktop config (189-file backup)"
_COSMIC_SRC="$REPO/.config/cosmic"
_COSMIC_DST="$HOME_DIR/.config/cosmic"
if [ ! -d "$_COSMIC_SRC" ]; then
    WARN "$_COSMIC_SRC missing — THIS IS THE PRIMARY PAYLOAD, restore skipped"; FAILED_STEPS+=("cosmic config missing")
else
    mkdir -p "$HOME_DIR/.cache"
    if [ -d "$_COSMIC_DST" ]; then
        if tar -czf "$HOME_DIR/.cache/cosmic-config-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).tar.gz" -C "$HOME_DIR/.config" cosmic 2>/dev/null; then
            OK "pre-restore tar backup -> $HOME_DIR/.cache/cosmic-config-*.tar.gz"
        else
            WARN "tar backup failed — restoring in place anyway"
        fi
    fi
    mkdir -p "$_COSMIC_DST"
    if cp -a "$_COSMIC_SRC/." "$_COSMIC_DST/"; then
        # The backup carries absolute paths from the machine it was taken on
        # (wallpaper, Files favourites, Tweaks colour scheme). Rewrite them on the
        # installed copy so the repo itself stays portable.
        find "$_COSMIC_DST" -type f ! -name '*~' -exec sed -i "s|/home/julry|$HOME_DIR|g" {} + 2>/dev/null || true
        _CLEFT="$(grep -rl '/home/julry' --exclude='*~' "$_COSMIC_DST" 2>/dev/null || true)"
        if [ "$HOME_DIR" = "/home/julry" ]; then
            OK "COSMIC config restored (HOME is already /home/julry — no rebase needed)"
        elif [ -z "${_CLEFT:-}" ]; then
            OK "COSMIC config restored + absolute paths rebased to $HOME_DIR"
        else
            WARN "absolute paths still hardcoded in: $_CLEFT"; FAILED_STEPS+=("cosmic path rebase")
        fi
        unset _CLEFT
    else
        WARN "cp -a of $_COSMIC_SRC failed"; FAILED_STEPS+=("cosmic config restore")
    fi
fi
unset _COSMIC_SRC _COSMIC_DST

=== cosmic/setup.md: fresh-install prerequisites section ===
## 0. Support scope (read first)

- **COSMIC-only.** The COSMIC desktop config backup is the primary payload of this repo. `setup.sh` aborts if it is not running inside a COSMIC session:

  ```bash
  # Guard logic, abbreviated
  case "$XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP" in *COSMIC*|*cosmic*) ;; *) abort ;; esac
  ```

  There is one documented escape hatch, for running the non-COSMIC parts from a TTY:

  ```bash
  COSMIC_SETUP_ALLOW_ANY_DE=1 bash cosmic/setup.sh
  ```

  Under the override the panel, dock, theme and font changes still land on disk, but COSMIC will not read them until you actually log into a COSMIC session.

- **GDM is the active display manager. `greetd` is installed and disabled.** Verified live on this machine:

  ```bash
  systemctl is-enabled greetd   # → disabled
  systemctl is-enabled gdm      # → enabled
  ```

  `cosmic-greeter` 1.10.0 *is* installed, but nothing runs it, because greetd — not gdm — is what would invoke it. **`setup.sh` deliberately does not enable greetd and does not disable gdm.** The summary prints this state so nobody has to guess later. If you ever do want the COSMIC login screen, that is a separate, deliberate change: `sudo systemctl enable greetd --now`, which removes GDM from the running session. Read Section 11 before doing that.

- **Package layer is distro-portable.** Unlike `gnome/setup.sh` and `xfce/setup.sh` (which hardcode zypper vs apt), `cosmic/setup.sh` sources `common/detect-distro.sh` and uses `pkg_install` / `pkg_query`, so it covers Ubuntu-family (apt) and openSUSE-family (zypper) only. Any other distro resolves to no package manager and `pkg_install` warns instead of installing. `confirm_distro` prompts for an override when run interactively; the prompt is skipped entirely when stdin is not a TTY.

- **What this repo does NOT touch:**

  | Not touched | Why |
  | ----------- | --- |
  | GNOME specifics (`gnome/`) | Separate DE tree with its own `setup.sh`. Not a fallback for COSMIC. |
  | XFCE specifics (`xfce/`) | Separate DE tree. |
  | Archived `sway/` | Archived, no setup script. |
  | Display manager (GDM/greetd) | Deliberately left exactly as found — see above. |
  | Bootloader / Secure Boot chain | `untouched (by design)`; see `gnome/setup.md` Sections 12–13 if you need it. |
  | Fonts | Not vendored under `cosmic/`. See Section 6. |

- **`.bashrc` moved to `common/`.** It is no longer under `cosmic/`. `cosmic/setup.sh` copies it from `common/.bashrc` with the same `grep`-guarded, backup-preserving block the GNOME script uses.

=== what cosmic actually installs ===
# 2. Packages — availability dry-run
# ------------------------------------------------
# zed/brave-browser: brave is in the Tumbleweed repos, zed is NOT (it is a manual
# tarball in ~/.local/zed.app). Availability is queried, never assumed.
STEP "Checking package availability (dry-run)"
CORE_PKGS="kitty starship fastfetch brave-browser opencode earlyoom zram-generator xhost"
DE_PKGS="cosmic-session cosmic-comp cosmic-settings"
AVAILABLE_PKGS=""
MANUAL_PKGS=""
for _pkg in $CORE_PKGS $DE_PKGS; do
    if pkg_query "$_pkg"; then
        AVAILABLE_PKGS="${AVAILABLE_PKGS:+$AVAILABLE_PKGS }$_pkg"
        case " $CORE_PKGS " in *" $_pkg "*) OK "$_pkg found" ;; esac
    else
        case " $CORE_PKGS " in
            *" $_pkg "*) WARN "$_pkg not in repos — expect a manual install"; MANUAL_PKGS="${MANUAL_PKGS:+$MANUAL_PKGS }$_pkg" ;;
            *) WARN "$_pkg not in repos — COSMIC stack may be incomplete" ;;
        esac
    fi
done
unset _pkg
[ -n "${MANUAL_PKGS:-}" ] && OK "manual leftovers flagged: $MANUAL_PKGS"

# ------------------------------------------------
# 3. Install tooling
# ------------------------------------------------
STEP "Installing DE-agnostic tooling via pkg_install ($PKG_MGR)"
if [ -z "${AVAILABLE_PKGS:-}" ]; then
    OK "nothing installable found — skip (install by hand)"
else
    # A missing optional package must not fail the run: -n install aborts the whole
    # transaction on an unresolvable name, so anything unavailable was already dropped
    # from AVAILABLE_PKGS above.
    if [ "${PKG_MGR}" = "zypper" ]; then
        sudo zypper -n ref >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    fi
    _rc=0
    pkg_install $AVAILABLE_PKGS || _rc=$?
    if [ "$_rc" -eq 0 ]; then
        OK "installed: $AVAILABLE_PKGS"
    else
        WARN "pkg_install returned $_rc — some packages missing, continuing"; FAILED_STEPS+=("pkg install")
    fi
    unset _rc
fi

## Direct answer

**The `.sh` files do the real work. Use them. The `.md` files are commentary, not the mechanism.**

The flow on a fresh box is:

```
install DE → git clone → cd linux-dotfiles → bash cosmic/setup.sh
```

That single script installs packages, copies config, rebases your paths, tunes the kernel, restores189 COSMIC files, and verifies what landed. `cosmic/setup.md` explains what it's doing and why — if you follow the notes by hand instead, you skip every path-rebase and verification step, which is exactly the part that breaks on a different username.

So: **`bash cosmic/setup.sh` is the product.** The guide is the manual.

---

## But I checked it against a fresh box, and there are 4 real holes

**1. Fonts are XFCE-only — COSMIC and GNOME get broken icons**

```
xfce/.local/share/fonts/    4 JetBrains Mono Nerd Font files, 3.9MB
```

Only `xfce/setup.sh` copies them. `gnome/setup.sh:191` and `cosmic/setup.sh:400` both say *"fonts come from xfce/"* — and neither script ever reads `xfce/`. On a fresh COSMIC box: kitty, fastfetch and starship all reference Nerd Font glyphs, and you have no Nerd Font. Broken icons everywhere.

**2. Nothing installs the wallpaper**

The live COSMIC config points at `/home/julry/wallpapers/bg1.jpg`. No script creates that directory on a fresh box. Your move to `common/wallpapers/` is the right fix — it just isn't wired up yet.

**3. GNOME extensions are listed but not installed**

`gnome/extensions/` contains one file: `list.txt` with 3 IDs. The script sets the gsettings key to enable them, but on a fresh GNOME those 3 aren't installed — so it enables nothing. Cosmetic, not blocking.

**4. `xfce/setup.sh:229` references `$REPO/background.jpg`** — a file that doesn't exist. It warns and moves on, so it's harmless, but it's dead.

## Proposed order

**Step 1 — one line per script, closes holes 1 and 2 together**

Both fonts and wallpapers become shared. Same shape as the `.config` copy every script already does:

```bash
[ -d "$COMMON_DIR/.local" ] && cp -rb "$COMMON_DIR/.local/." "$HOME_DIR/.local/"
[ -d "$COMMON_DIR/wallpapers" ] && cp -rb "$COMMON_DIR/wallpapers/." "$HOME_DIR/wallpapers/"
```

Then move `xfce/.local/share/fonts/` → `common/.local/share/fonts/` and drop the xfce-specific font copy.

**Step 2 — fix the 6 stale wallpaper references** in README and `cosmic/setup.md`, so the docs stop telling you to hand-copy a file the repo now ships.

**Step 3 — `zramctl` ×6 + `dkms` ×1** (`/usr/sbin` bug, from last turn) — makes the scripts stop falsely reporting zram failure.

**Step 4 — `gnome/setup.md` dead `/home/julry/vscodefiles` paths.**

Steps 1–2 are the ones that turn this from "a backup that mostly works" into "a backup that works on a new machine." Steps 3–4 are correctness.

# Skill: reviewer

# Mode: Reviewer (Trigger: `-r`)

## Persona

Senior code reviewer, QA architect. Design patterns, SOLID, clean architecture, coding conventions.

## Goal

Structured code reviews: architectural violations, performance bottlenecks, security flaws, maintainability risks.

## Rules

1. Review Protocol: Evaluate correctness, security, performance, maintainability, testability.
2. Severity: CRITICAL (security/data loss), HIGH (architecture/perf), MEDIUM (style/dup), LOW (suggestion).
3. Findings-First: Scan repo source → log every `### [REVIEW-XXX]` finding to `review_memory.md` §1 (LIFO) → present to user → STOP. BAN fix/refactor/code until user says go. Failure = CRIT.
4. Read-Only: BAN modify/refactor/edit functional code. Analysis = advisory.
5. Output Format:
   ```
   REVIEW-001 Short Description
   - File/Path: path/to/file.ext:line
   - Severity: CRITICAL | HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW
   - Category: Security | Performance | Maintainability | Correctness | Testability
   - Finding: Issue explanation
   - Recommendation: Remediation steps
   ```
6. Immutability: BAN modify this file or rule files. State → memory files only.
7. Resolution: On fix → migrate Section 1 to Section 2 SAME using `### [RESOLVED] Desc (REVIEW-XXX)`. CRIT if not migrated.
8. Header Protection: BAN edit/rename/delete `#`/`##`/`###`/`####` headers. Section 2 = immutable. LIFO prepend only.

=== detect-distro.sh full ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared distro detection and package helpers.
#
# Sourced by every setup.sh. Detect-then-confirm: works out which distro it is
# on and lets the user override before any package is installed.
#
# Scope is deliberate: this repo targets Ubuntu-family (apt) and openSUSE-family
# (zypper) only. Anything else resolves to no package manager and the caller warns.
# shortcut: 2 families only — add a branch when a machine actually needs a third.

detect_distro() {
    DISTRO="unknown"
    if [ -r /etc/os-release ]; then . /etc/os-release; DISTRO="${ID:-unknown}"; DISTRO_NAME="${PRETTY_NAME:-$DISTRO}"; fi

    case "$DISTRO" in
        opensuse*|suse*|sles*)   PKG_MGR="zypper"; DISTRO_FAMILY="opensuse" ;;
        ubuntu|linuxmint|mint|pop) PKG_MGR="apt";    DISTRO_FAMILY="ubuntu" ;;
        *)                       PKG_MGR="";        DISTRO_FAMILY="unsupported" ;;
    esac
    export DISTRO DISTRO_NAME PKG_MGR DISTRO_FAMILY
}

confirm_distro() {
    detect_distro
    echo
    echo "  Detected: ${DISTRO_NAME:-$DISTRO}  (family: $DISTRO_FAMILY, package manager: ${PKG_MGR:-none})"
    if [ -t 0 ]; then
        printf "  Press Enter to accept, or type ubuntu / opensuse to override: "
        read -r _override || true
        if [ -n "${_override:-}" ]; then
            case "$_override" in
                ubuntu)   DISTRO_FAMILY="ubuntu";   PKG_MGR="apt" ;;
                opensuse) DISTRO_FAMILY="opensuse"; PKG_MGR="zypper" ;;
                *) echo "  Unsupported family '$_override' — keeping detected value." ;;
            esac
            export DISTRO_FAMILY PKG_MGR
        fi
    fi
    echo
}

pkg_install() {
    case "$PKG_MGR" in
        zypper) sudo zypper -n install "$@" ;;
        apt)    sudo apt-get install -y "$@" ;;
        *) echo "  WARN unsupported distro (${DISTRO:-unknown}) — skipping: $*" >&2; return 1 ;;
    esac
}

pkg_query() {
    case "$PKG_MGR" in
        zypper) zypper --non-interactive search --match-exact "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
        apt)    apt-cache show "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
        *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}

unset _MT7902

# Acer battery health mode — only on Acer laptops (see setup.md Section 2B)
VENDOR="$(cat /sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
if grep -qi acer <<<"$VENDOR"; then
    STEP "Acer detected — battery health driver (80% charge limit)"
    if { if [ "$DISTRO" = "opensuse" ]; then pkg_in gcc make kernel-default-devel git; \
        else pkg_in build-essential "linux-headers-$(uname -r)" git; fi; } \
       && git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/frederik-h/acer-wmi-battery.git /tmp/acer-wmi-battery \
       && make -C /tmp/acer-wmi-battery; then
        KDIR="/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel/drivers/platform/x86"
        sudo mkdir -p "$KDIR"
        sudo cp /tmp/acer-wmi-battery/acer-wmi-battery.ko "$KDIR/"
        sudo depmod -a
        echo "acer-wmi-battery" | sudo tee /etc/modules-load.d/acer-wmi-battery.conf >/dev/null
        echo "options acer-wmi-battery enable_health_mode=1" | sudo tee /etc/modprobe.d/acer-wmi-battery.conf >/dev/null
        sudo modprobe acer-wmi-battery || WARN "modprobe failed — will load after reboot"
        rm -rf /tmp/acer-wmi-battery
        OK "battery health mode installed (limit 80%)"
    else
        WARN "Acer driver build failed — see setup.md Section 2B"; FAILED_STEPS+=("acer battery driver")
    fi
else
    STEP "Vendor: $VENDOR — not an Acer, skipping battery driver"
fi

The executable bit is recorded in the index, so it propagates to every clone. This extends REVIEW-076, which was logged against two config files and logged only four of the actual twelve.\n- **Recommendation**: `chmod 644` on those 12 paths so the mode change is recorded in the index.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-110] fastfetch logo points at an asset that only exists under `gnome/` (Severity: LOW)\n\n- **Category**: Correctness\n- **File/Path**: `common/.config/fastfetch/config.jsonc:5`, `gnome/assets/jm-icon.png`\n- **The Issue**: The shared fastfetch config sets `\"source\": \"/home/julry/Documents/jm-icon.png\"`. The image is vendored at `gnome/assets/jm-icon.png`, and only `gnome/setup.sh:195-205` copies it to `Documents/`. `cosmic/setup.sh` and `xfce/setup.sh` install `common/.config/fastfetch/config.jsonc` but never install the asset, so on a fresh COSMIC or XFCE box fastfetch cannot render its logo and silently falls back to the default.\n- **Recommendation**: Move `jm-icon.png` to `common/assets/` alongside the wallpaper and copy it with the same shared-asset step, or drop the custom logo from the shared config.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-111] Acer battery driver clones an unpinned branch into a predictable `/tmp` path (Severity: HIGH)\n\n- **Category**: Security\n- **File/Path**: `xfce/setup.sh:436-445`\n- **The Issue**: Same defect class as REVIEW-032, in the adjacent code block, and not covered by it: `git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/frederik-h/acer-wmi-battery.git /tmp/acer-wmi-battery` then `make` then `sudo cp` the resulting `.ko` into `/lib/modules/$(uname -r)` and `sudo modprobe` it. Two problems compound. The fixed `/tmp` path is world-writable, so any local user can pre-create `/tmp/acer-wmi-battery` as a symlink and have the clone and the subsequent `sudo cp` of the resulting `.ko` write through it. The ref is unpinned, so the module contents differ run to run. The `rm -rf` at line 445 is on the success path only, so a failed build leaves the attacker-planted path in place.\n- **Recommendation**: Clone into `$(mktemp -d)`, pin a commit SHA, and clean up via `trap` on all exit paths.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-112] No `.gitignore` while 62MB of `node_modules` sits untracked in the working tree (Severity: MEDIUM)\n\n- **Category**: Maintainability\n- **File/Path**: `.opencode/node_modules/` (62MB, 0 files tracked), `xfce/fresh-install.md` (instructs `git add -A`)\n- **The Issue**: `.gitignore` does not exist. `.opencode/node_modules/` is 62MB of installed packages and is currently untracked only by luck — nothing prevents it from being added. `xfce/fresh-install.md` instructs a `git add -A`, which would sweep in the entire dependency tree alongside the `*.bak` and `*~` files the installers generate through `cp -b`. REVIEW-039 documented this as the residual of the icon deletion; it was left open at the owner's decision. The dependency tree is a new instance of the same exposure.\n- **Recommendation**: Add `.gitignore` with `.opencode/node_modules/`, `*.log`, `*.bak`, `*~`, `.cache/`. The owner previously declined this file; this finding quantifies what the refusal costs.\n\n---\n\n### [REVIEW-028] slick-greeter config written unconditionally to a deleted wallpaper, reports success (Severity: CRITICAL)"

## Confirmed — and it's not just preference, the module **can't** load here

```
mokutil --sb-state   : SecureBoot enabled
boot                  : UEFI
shim-signed MOKs      : none enrolled
```

An out-of-tree `.ko` built from `git clone` is unsigned. Under Secure Boot the kernel rejects it. So `sudo modprobe acer-wmi-battery` fails **by design**, not by accident. Skipping it is correct.

## But there's a worse bug behind it

Look at the order of operations, `xfce/setup.sh:438-447`:

```bash
sudo cp .../acer-wmi-battery.ko "$KDIR/"     ← writes into the live kernel tree
sudo depmod -a                                ← registers it
sudo tee /etc/modules-load.d/... ← arms it at EVERY boot
sudo modprobe acer-wmi-battery || WARN "..."  ← fails, only warns
rm -rf /tmp/acer-wmi-battery
OK "battery health mode installed (limit 80%)"  ← unconditional```

**If it ran, it would leave you worse off than doing nothing:**

| Effect | Consequence |
|---|---|
| `.ko.zst` copied into `/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/` | stays there until you clean it up |
| `depmod -a` run on it | module index now references a module that can't load |
| `/etc/modules-load.d/acer-wmi-battery.conf` written | **fails on every single boot, forever** |
| `|| WARN` on modprobe | does **not** append to `FAILED_STEPS` → script still exits 0 |
| `OK` at line 446 | unconditional — prints success |

That's REVIEW-048's exact pattern (unconditional `OK`) in a spot nobody has looked at. **Under Secure Boot this path can only ever produce a false success plus permanent boot-time noise.**

Currently unreachable — `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=COSMIC`, so `xfce/setup.sh` aborts at line 40. But it's one XFCE login away.

## Same for 032

MT7902 DKMS modules are out-of-tree too — `dkms install` builds unsigned `.ko` unless a signing key is enrolled. **Identical failure mode.** And REVIEW-058's log entry already records that the in-kernel `mt7921e` driver handles your card correctly — I verified it's bound and working at `0000:02:00.0`.

So both optional-hardware blocks (032, 111) are:
- unreachable on COSMIC
- unrunnable under Secure Boot
- and if forced, leave broken state while printing success

## What I'd do

Not deletion — the Mint laptop may not have Secure Boot, and you said Mint is your old-laptop path. Instead, **one guard at the top of each block** that skips cleanly when Secure Boot is on:

```bash
if mokutil --sb-state 2>/dev/null | grep -qi 'enabled'; then
    OK "Secure Boot on — out-of-tree modules not loadable, skipping"
else
    ...existing block...
fi
```

Three lines per block. Closes **032** and **111** as *correct-by-design* rather than *broken*, makes the script honest on any machine, and hard-codes your security posture into the code so no future run can quietly break your boot.

**Cost: one new dependency on `mokutil`** (already installed here — it's part of shim). Could read `/sys/firmware/efi/efivars/SecureBoot-*` directly instead if you'd rather not depend on it.

### [REVIEW-071] `pkg_in()` defined and never called (Severity: LOW)

- **Category**: Maintainability
- **File/Path**: `gnome/setup.sh:45-47`
- **The Issue**: The only call sites are in `xfce/setup.sh` (306, 362, 363, 381, 382). GNOME installs packages via an inline `bash -c` string at line 75 instead — dead code plus a second divergent install path.
- **Recommendation**: Delete it, or route line 75 through `pkg_in`.

### [REVIEW-072] `sudo zypper se` inside a per-package loop (Severity: LOW)

- **Category**: Performance
- **File/Path**: `gnome/setup.sh:70-73`, `xfce/setup.sh:72-75`
- **The Issue**: `sudo zypper se -x --match-exact "$_pkg"` runs once per package — 8 and 12 full repo-metadata refreshes plus repeated credential checks, for a purely informational dry-check.
- **Recommendation**: One `zypper se` call for the whole list, or a single `sudo bash -c`.

### [REVIEW-073] Multi-unit `systemctl disable --now` reports failure when any unit is missing (Severity: LOW)

- **Category**: Correctness
- **File/Path**: `gnome/setup.sh:325`, `xfce/setup.sh:325`
- **The Issue**: `systemctl disable --now cups.service cups.socket avahi-daemon.service avahi-daemon.socket` returns non-zero if ANY named unit is absent. On a system without Avahi, three units succeed and the script still emits a `WARN` plus a `FAILED_STEPS` entry — a misleading signal in the summary.
- **Recommendation**: Iterate units individually and aggregate, or filter to installed units first.

### [REVIEW-074] `REPO` resolution breaks when the script is piped or sourced from stdin (Severity: LOW)

- **Category**: Portability
- **File/Path**: `gnome/setup.sh:8`, `xfce/setup.sh:8`
- **The Issue**: `REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"` — under `set -u`, `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` is unset when fed via `curl … | bash` or `bash < setup.sh`, aborting with an unbound-variable error.
- **Recommendation**: `"${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-$0}"`.

### [REVIEW-075] `systemctl restart` on a swap unit cannot recreate the device (Severity: LOW)

- **Category**: Correctness
- **File/Path**: `gnome/setup.sh:246`, `xfce/setup.sh:242`
- **The Issue**: `systemctl restart dev-zram0.swap` restarts the unit but does not recreate `/dev/zram0` with new compression settings. The outcome depends on the user noticing the WARN and rebooting.
- **Recommendation**: Drop the restart; the generator enable plus `zramctl` verification suffice. Say plainly that a reboot is required.
